On 9 September, Elizabeth Moselakgomo left her home in east Johannesburg to go for a run.

When the 38 year-old mother didn’t return home, her eight-year-old daughter told relatives, who then contacted police. During her disappearance, family and friends made public appeals to help find her, the case went viral on social media and police launched a task force to investigate.

Five days after she vanished, her body was discovered in a park, half-naked and bruised.

Ms Moselakgomo was one of nine women found dead in the region in recent months in similar circumstances. The first body was discovered in July, naked and bound with cable ties, with two more found shortly after but drawing little attention at the time.

open image in gallery A memorial run held in honour of Elizabeth Moselakgomo, one of several women killed in a series of murders near Johannesburg ( Reuters )

“We cannot continue picking up bodies,” said Tebello Mosikili, the deputy police chief, at the scene of the discovery in Dawn Park on Thursday.

It is not yet clear if the cases are connected and police have yet to rule out a potential serial killer.

Regardless, South African women and advocacy groups say the cases highlight the wider epidemic of femicide across the country, with widespread anger that more has not been done to tackle the problem.

In November 2025, President Cyril Ramaphosa officially declared gender-based violence and femicide a national disaster, after campaigning by Women For Change.

According to official statistics from the South African Police Service (SAPS), at least 5,578 women were murdered in a year in South Africa between March 2023 and March 2024, after which figures have not been released.

The UN Office on Drugs and Crime says that the female homicide rate in South Africa is almost six times the global average at 12.2 per 100,000 women in 2022, with the global average being 2.2.

Police advised women not to run or walk alone in response to the recent killings, prompting swift backlash. President Ramaphosa promised “no stone would be left unturned” in the quest for answers.

Merlize Jogiat, operations and advocacy manager at Women For Change, says that the charity received 3,000 requests for support between Monday and Wednesday this week alone.

open image in gallery Elizabeth Moselakgomo was found dead after she went missing following a run ( South Africa Police Service )

Since launching their Survivor Support Line in April 2026, they have had more than 40,000 messages from women and girls on issues including domestic violence and child sexual abuse, as well as from the families of femicide victims.

“We speak to families of femicide victims, almost on a daily basis,” says Jogiat. “Rape cases are through the roof. I don’t know a single woman that has not to some degree been sexually harassed, abused, or raped.”

In east Johannesburg, she says that the situation is dire. Women have told her that they are scared to leave their homes, are travelling in groups, and are even learning to operate guns for self-defence.

“As a woman, I’m scared,” writes one woman who works in the area in a text to Merlize. “I have three girls of my own and I’m afraid for them as well as ALL my nieces. It’s like we can’t go to the shop alone anymore, we have to go in pairs or a group.

“It’s truly been unsettling. Then there’s the anger at this person (or people) targeting women. They feel we’re the weaker sex so they can overpower us.”

Another woman who lives in an area closest to where the bodies were found, sent a picture of herself signing up for a gun course as she advised others to do the same.

open image in gallery South Africa declared a national emergency on gender-based violence last year ( Reuters )

South Africa’s gender commissioner says women are being “hunted” and Jogiat says that violence against women is a “crisis” but campaigners say not enough is being done.

The country’s minister for women, youth and persons with disabilities, Sindisiwe Chikunga, said on Friday the government’s policies for tackling gender-based violence against women remain largely unfunded.

This is reflected in the DNA backlog, with only 3.5 per cent of samples being processed within the legislated 30-day period. Over 175,000 individual samples remain untested and waiting, according to Action Society.

Cultural norms and a history of apartheid, which “fundamentally broke the men in this country”, also play a part, as Jogiat says men sought to exert control over women in response.

“We’re terrified all of the time,” says Jogiat, who fears for her personal safety as well as that of her 16-year-old daughter. “As South African women, we have gotten accustomed to our safety always being in jeopardy.

“Around the world, women have to look out for themselves, but we have to take it up a notch.

“We are watching our backs when we walk in the street in the morning, now we have the police telling us we need to run in groups. One of my friends said the other day, ‘I’m too afraid to go for a coffee and wear this particular thing because I don’t know what kind of attention I’m getting.’

“I've had an incident in Johannesburg when I was there with a guy pulling over on the side of the road and wanting to give me a ride, just randomly. Kidnappings have also gone up quite substantially.”

She worries for her daughter if she does not hear from her for a couple of hours. “I don’t even want to leave my house,” she said.

But Jogiat believes the onus is on the government to find a way through the crisis beyond “PR”.

“We’ve been screaming about this issue for over 10 years,” she says. “All the promises that they give us never translate to anything on the ground.”

She says that even simple issues such as bail conditions for alleged sex offenders and abusers are not enforced and a suspect can be released for as little as £250.

“People who are going through abusive divorces, nine times out of 10, the court is believing the abuser over the victim,” she says. “A man’s word trumps a woman’s abuse in this country.”

Jogiat believes that the recent discoveries were made due to a police presence in the search for Elizabeth and that they may never have been found otherwise.

“They were forced to cut the grass and found the decomposing bodies,” she says.

Meanwhile, the families of the victims are still desperate for answers.

Elizabeth’s aunt, Vinah Moselakgomo, told ENCA: “It's difficult for Elizabeth’s eight-year-old to come to terms with what’s happened, as she still keeps asking where her mother is.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

News.title: Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash
News.content:
Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The record books will show that this meeting, a proper Test full of ebbs and flows, was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level of professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

“The plan on the field at the last scrum was to go for the win,” Canada captain Sophie de Goede said. “And then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. In that moment you have to trust your coach and your coaching staff, and we’ll have a discussion about it later. If we had given away a penalty off the next breakdown, we’d be sitting here going, ‘Why didn’t you kick it out?’”

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance, in a tale which was not too dissimilar to last week. The hosts came second in the physical battle, too, which was uncharacteristic of them; losing Hannah Botterman to a shoulder injury did not help, either. All told, Canada just looked as though they wanted it a little bit more and maybe this was the wake-up call the Red Roses needed: when you are at the top, and at the top by a margin, every team want to be the one to dethrone you.

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

News.title: Global fund utilises AI to tackle malaria, TB, and HIV amid aid cuts
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to soften the blow from aid cuts, according to one of the world’s biggest development funds.

The Global Fund, which raises and invests billions of pounds to reduce the burden of HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria globally says new AI-driven products like portable pregnancy scanners are helping to mitigate the funding gap.

“[We] have adapted pretty quickly to the changes in the funding environment; it has undoubtedly had negative impacts on health outcomes [...], but in some ways, the resilience of life-saving services has been remarkable,” Peter Sands, the executive director of the Global Fund, told The Telegraph.

The Global Fund is managing a $6 billion (£4.4bn) shortfall for the period 2026 to 2028 and has been forced to make difficult decisions to continue their work, it confirmed this week.

The gap comes as Western governments shift money from foreign aid to defence. The UK reduced its contribution to the fund by 15 per cent last year to £850 million, down from £1 billion.

But Mr Sands said investments in tools to tackle infectious diseases – including those driven by AI – are starting to pay off.

“Innovation is absolutely part of the answer when money is short. One of the few ways you can get to make the money go further is to have a better tool, a better way of doing things,” Mr Sands said.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players
News.content:
Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

Sports.title: England star handed cruel new injury blow just days after being called up by Thomas Tuchel to latest squad
Sports.content:
Next

TINO LIVRAMENTO is set to pull out of England duty after suffering a fresh injury blow.

The Newcastle full-back’s World Cup was cruelly cut-short this summer due to a calf issue.



The 23-year-old finally returned to action a fortnight ago as sub in Toon’s 2-2 draw with Bournemouth.

Despite only making two substitute appearances since, Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel still called him up this week for the upcoming Nations League games.



Luckless Livramento was set to start for the injury-hit Mags on Saturday against Hull until he suffered an unspecified injury in training on Friday.

And now boss Matthias Jaissle is praying it is nothing long-term.

He said: “He suffered discomfort after training. He will have an MRI scan but that’s all from my side.”

Sports.title: Dortmund boss Niko Kovac holds back tears as he is told about death of close friend Peter Hermann live on German TV
Sports.content:
'deeply saddened' Dortmund boss Niko Kovac holds back tears as he is told about death of close friend Peter Hermann live on German TV







Next

BORUSSIA DORTMUND manager Niko Kovac held back tears before cancelling an interview when he found out about the tragic death of close friend and assistant, Peter Hermann.

Kovac, 54, was conducting an interview with Sky Sport Germany following Dortmund’s 1-0 win at Stuttgart when he was told of the news.



The Dortmund boss was visibly distressed by the announcement as presenter Sebastian Hellmann told him the news.

He was told the news during the interview before relaying it to Kovac and pundits Lothar Matthaus and Julia Simic.



Reacting to the news, Kovac said: “It leaves me a little short of breath.

“One or two months ago I was still trying to speak to him, that was no longer possible at all.

“Unfortunately his illness was incurable.

“I am deeply saddened, a good person has left us.”

Kovac had said that when he tried to speak to his old friend before, his call was answered by Hermann’s daughter.

Hermann died at the age of 74 after a long battle against neurodegenerative illness amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).



He was an assistant to Jupp Heynckes when Bayern Munich won their first treble in 2013, and went back to Bayern when Heynckes returned in 2017, before staying on for a further year when Kovac took charge.

He had been an assistant in over 1,000 matches for various clubs including Schalke, Hamburg, Bayer Leverkusen and Dortmund.

Following his Sky interview, a distraught Kovac cancelled a media appearance with ZDF’s Aktuelles Sportstudio, as revealed by presenter Katrin Müller-Hohenstein on Saturday evening.

Kovac fought back tears during his post-match press conference, saying: “From me and also from my brother, our sincere condolences to Peter’s family.



“A great man has left us.

“Not only as an assistant coach in Munich, but also as assistant coach when I was still a player in Leverkusen.

“Really a shock.”

Sports.title: Ezri Konsa says Arsenal have a lot to learn and fix after shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton ends winning start

Next

EZRI KONSA says Arsenal have “a lot to learn and fix” after Brighton ended their perfect start to the season.

The Gunners were beaten 3-0 by the Seagulls on Saturday as the defence of their Premier League crown suffered its first setback.



Defender Konsa believes there were “no excuses” for the poor performance and the squad must use the upcoming international break to reset.

The England star said: “We have high standards here and we let them go.



“There are no excuses. We just weren’t good enough.

“But it is important we use this time now to reflect as individuals, to know that when we do come back there is a lot to learn and fix from this game.

“We were very disappointed to lose and to concede three goals is not like us. As a defender, I pride myself on keeping clean sheets.

“We did not do that to the best of our abilities. We have to move on very quickly and focus on the game after the break.”

Arsenal had won seven matches on the spin in all competitions before their defeat at the Amex.

Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas scored long-range efforts before half time, and Chema Andres added a third around the hour mark from a corner.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Gunners’ defending was all over the place as they conceded more goals during one afternoon than in their previous nine Prem games combined.

Konsa said: “We conceded two goals from outside of the box. They were two very good strikes.

“But there were moments in those two goals where we could have pressed the ball more, put more pressure on the ball.

“It’s the Premier League, when you give quality players outside the box time and they shoot, it can go in.

“These are lessons that we need to learn from. We are still growing, still improving and we only want to get better.”



Arsenal return to action after the international break when they host Leeds on October 10.

And midfielder Bruno Guimaraes is expecting them to come back fired up after a dismal day at Brighton.

The Brazil star said: “Now we have to focus on the national teams but when we come back, we have to ensure this does not happen again.

“We have to forget this and improve, we have to say sorry to the fans because it wasn’t good enough.

“We cannot accept this while wearing this shirt of a champion.”

Sports.title: Micah Richards opens up about dad's death and tough decision to carry on with live BBC punditry
Sports.content:
Micah Richards opens up about dad's death and tough decision to carry on with live BBC punditry

Micah Richards' father died not long before he went on air to provide punditry for the BBC during England's World Cup semi-final against Argentina

View 3 Images Micah Richards has spoken about his father's death and the tough decision to go live on the BBC soon after (Image: Getty)

Micah Richards has opened up about carrying on with his punditry duties at the World Cup for the BBC after learning of his father's death. The former Manchester City star's dad, Lincoln, died shortly before Richards went on air for England's semi-final in the summer against Argentina.

‌



Richards is known as one of English football's most cheerful and recognisable pundits. Since ending his playing career in 2019, which constituted spells at City, Fiorentina and Aston Villa, he has established himself as a notable voice across CBS and Sky Sports, as well as on podcast platforms.

‌



He is also a regular on the BBC and Match of the Day. But while covering the World Cup for the corporation this summer, his world was turned upside down by his father Lincoln's passing on July 15.

‌



Richards was told of his dad's death shortly before he was due to go on air for the semi-final clash. Bravely, he made the decision to carry on with his punditry duties in the wake of the devastating news.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Richards has now spoken out about the heartbreaking ordeal. He admits that he was trying to hold himself together whilst on live television and how lead presenter Mark Chapman helped him through it.

‌



View 3 Images Richards announced his father's death in a heartbreaking post on social media (Image: @micahrichards/Instagram)

"On the day it happened, my brother rang me before the semi-final and I'm going into it thinking, 'How am I going to perform here? How am I going to act?'" Richards told The Sunday Times.

"I was on the phone to Chappers [Chapman] for an hour. And he was saying, 'Your dad would have wanted you to do it. This is what you've worked for since you've come into punditry.' I didn't want to tell Joe and Wayne, because I've known Joe since I was 17 and didn't want to affect them.

‌



"Chappers said, 'If in the first ten minutes you're having a wobble, let me know and we can just continue with the rest of the guys.' If it wasn't for him, I wouldn't have got through it. One hundred per cent. And it was weird because when I'm on camera, I'm sort of loud and obnoxious at times, but if you watch the footage, I keep tapping my foot. I was just trying to hold it together."

Tributes and support poured in for Richards after he took to social media to confirm the news of his father's death. He later stated that Lincoln had not been well for some time.

"Two years before he passed, I sort of saw it coming," continued Richards. "I didn't think it would be so soon, but he was on a road and he couldn't get out of it. And what was more heartbreaking is I couldn't do anything.

Article continues below

View 3 Images The ex-England full-back battled through the broadcast (Image: BBC)

"I was probably with him more than anyone in my life growing up and then he sort of took a turn for the worse where he was drinking at the time and I'd seen the road he was going down.

"It had already gone so far. So all the stuff he had done for me, I couldn't now give my input to him, help him—and that was the saddest thing. But in terms of impact he made, he was just unbelievable. I couldn't have asked for anything more."

Sports.title: Coleen Rooney reveals what husband Wayne is really like as she names four key traits

Coleen Rooney reveals what husband Wayne is really like as she names four key traits

Wayne Rooney's wife Coleen has shone a candid light on her husband's personality ahead of the launch of the upcoming Disney+ docu-series The Real Rooneys

View 3 Images Coleen Rooney says husband Wayne has a short temper (Image: SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Coleen Rooney has lifted the lid on what husband Wayne is really like behind closed doors - and admitted the England legend can have a short temper.

‌



The couple, who have been together since they were teenagers, opened up about their everyday dynamic in a candid new interview, revealing the relatable domestic squabbles that keep their household ticking.

‌



Despite navigating a number of highly publicised challenges and intense media scrutiny over their two decades together, the pair showed they still share a deep bond and a cheeky sense of humour.

‌



Coleen didn't hold back when asked to describe the former Manchester United striker's true personality. "Wayne is funny and laid-back. He can be a charmer, but can have a short temper," she told the Guardian.

When asked if he agreed with his wife's assessment, Wayne playfully replied: "Erm, the first three." But it didn't take long for the root of his occasional frustration to be exposed: waiting for Coleen.

‌



"He can be impatient, waiting around for things," Coleen explained. Wayne was quick to clarify exactly who he was usually waiting for. "For you," he fired back. "When we're getting up to go somewhere, I'm always early. If we're getting picked up to go somewhere and we're leaving the house at 6pm, I'll be ready by 5.15-5.30."

The relatable spat shows a different side to the couple, whose marriage has survived its fair share of storms in the spotlight. Over the years, they have had to weather their share of personal hurdles and relationship ups and downs, yet they made it clear their partnership remains resilient.

View 3 Images The Real Rooneys premieres on Disney+ later this month (Image: DISNEY)

‌



Later in the interview, the tables were turned on the football icon when he was asked to describe the real Coleen. Wayne couldn't hide his admiration for the mother of his four boys, praising her for keeping the busy Rooney household running smoothly.

"Very caring, very efficient in terms of what she does for us as a family," Wayne gushed. "She takes care of everything, which allows me to mess around a bit more with the kids."

The pair also couldn't resist a playful dig at each other's sense of humour. Wayne cheekily claimed his wife doesn't have one, declaring his own love for classic British comedy like Fawlty Towers and Only Fools and Horses.

‌



View 3 Images Wayne and Coleen live with their four sons, Kai, Klay, Kit and Cass in Cheshire (Image: @coleen_rooney/Instagram)

The couple did admit they are currently enjoying a rare spell of peace, revealing they are on "a good run" and haven't had a proper row in weeks. Though former England captain Wayne confessed that might just be down to his own survival tactic - keeping his mouth shut because he knows he stands no chance of winning.

"It's more you shouting at me and me just taking it," Wayne quipped, with Coleen confirming: "He goes quiet."

Article continues below

Laying out his white flag, Wayne added: "I'm never going to win the argument. If I start arguing back, it will just continue, so I'm man enough to accept it; let her get it off her chest. I don't think I've ever won an argument with her."

The candid marital insights come ahead of their new Disney+ docuseries The Real Rooneys, which offers fans an unprecedented look into the private home life of Wayne, Coleen and their four sons - Kai, Klay, Kit and Cass.

The Real Rooneys (Episodes 1–8) launches on Disney+ on September 24.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa in agreement over 'unacceptable' Arsenal defeat
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa in agreement over 'unacceptable' Arsenal defeat

BRIGHTON 3-0 ARSENAL: Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa both suffered their first defeats since joining the Premier League champions, who were put to the sword by Fabian Hurzeler's high-flying Seagulls at the Amex on Saturday

View 3 Images Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes both suffered their first defeat as Arsenal plaeyrs

Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa haven't been at Arsenal long - but both already know Saturday's 3-0 defeat at Brighton was "not acceptable" by the club's standards.

‌



The Brazilian midfield maestro, who failed to impress on his first Premier League start for the Gunners, insists a similar display cannot ever be repeated if Mikel Arteta's champions are to retain the title this term.

‌



He said: "We were not good enough, so far off our level this time. We are very disappointed, we have to learn from our mistakes because today we were far away off our level.

‌



"We were too sloppy with the ball; we didn't win any duels. We cannot accept this while wearing this shirt of a champion and we want to win the game.

"We cannot repeat this; it's a lesson for us because I think we've been on a good run so far. We've won every game but not this one. Like I said, it's one to forget for us but we have to learn from what happened today."

Declan Rice escapes red card with late kick out in Arsenal capitulation READ MORE :

After the game, Arteta claimed he knew Arsenal were not at the races following their first throw-in of the contest.

‌



Guimaraes admits the squad has been left to rue failing to close down both Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas for Brighton's two first-half goals.

"We gave them too much time on the ball, we know the quality that they have," said Guimaraes. "They were two amazing shots to be fair but we can do better and we have to do better.

"We cannot give them too much space, we cannot lose the ball in a dangerous area and like I said, bad day, I've not been too long here but it feels like we can't accept this."

‌



View 3 Images Chema Andres netted Brighton's third against Arsenal (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Arsenal now have to wait three weeks until they can respond at home to Leeds. However, Guimaraes, who fired home a stunner in the recent 2-0 triumph at Sunderland, doesn't want to get too down over his promising start to life in N5 following his £75million summer transfer from Newcastle.

He continued: "I have to adapt, and I think I've been doing great to be fair but I think today is one to forget for me and the whole team.

‌



"Today was a bad day at the office for everyone. I think I'm quite good in terms of adaptation with the club, I'm getting there.

"Now we have to focus on the national teams but when we come back, we have to ensure this does not happen again.

"We have to learn from our mistakes, wearing this shirt this is not acceptable, this is not the level we want but now we have time to focus on the national team, and when we come back, we have to win games. We have to forget this and improve, we have to say sorry to the fans because it wasn't good enough."

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal came unstuck at Brighton, who ran riot

Fellow newcomer Konsa was in agreement with Guimaraes that Arsenal's performance was simply not up to scratch.

He stated: “It wasn’t good enough. We have high standards here and we let them go today. But it is important we use this time now to reflect as individuals, to know that when we do come back there is a lot to learn and a lot to fix from this game.

‌



“We are very disappointed to lose and to concede three goals is not like us. As a defender, I pride myself on keeping clean sheets. We did not do that to the best of our abilities. We have to move on very quickly and focus on the game after the break.

“We conceded two goals from outside of the box. They were two very good strikes. But there were moments in those two goals where we could have pressed the ball more, put more pressure on the ball.

“It’s the Premier League, when you give quality players outside the box time and they shoot, it can go in. These are lessons that we need to learn from. We are still growing, still improving and we only want to get better.”

Townsend has now taken to social media to poke fun at what happened. Resharing an earlier post of his on his Instagram story, which read: "WTF is Stoke away" with clips of him enjoying life in Thailand, he added: "Turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all (laughing emoji) swipe to see why."

The following slide shows footage of him being flattened by the roller. He has also shared other posts making light of the episode, including being dubbed "the king of memes in Thai League history. " He added: "Trust me" with four laughing emojis.

‌



Townsend signed for PT Prachuap last month on a contract running until next summer. He made his bow in the 1-0 defeat to Rayong FC earlier this month and has since featured twice more for the club, including as a late substitute against Pattani.

The winger spent the previous campaign with Thai outfit Kanchanaburi, where he clocked up 30 appearances, netting three goals and laying on six assists. He has also had a stint in Turkey with Antalyaspor.

‌



Shedding light on his decision to head to Thailand in an interview with TalkSPORT, he said: "Towards the back end of last season, I was playing in Turkey, and I hadn't been paid a few months' salary.

"The club said to me 'you can take your salary - but you're never going to play for the club again' so I took the salary.

"I hadn't played since March, got a bit frustrated, so in the summer I said to Marlon [my agent] I don't care where I go, just take me somewhere nice, interesting and tropical.

‌



"He came back with one or two options in Europe but for some reason my gut was just really interested about the option in Thailand."

During his time in England, Townsend turned out for a string of clubs on both loan and permanent arrangements. Roy Hodgson handed him his international bow in 2013, and he went on to earn a further 12 caps, with his final outing for the Three Lions coming in a 2-2 friendly against Spain in November 2016.

Over the summer, he took on punditry and co-commentary duties for ITV during the World Cup in North America, giving his Instagram followers a behind-the-scenes glimpse into the experience through daily video diaries.

Sports.title: Broad excited at what Fleming can do for Root's captaincy
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad is excited at what new England Test coach Stephen Fleming can bring to Joe Root's captaincy as the New Zealander prepares for his first assignment in the role in South Africa this winter.

Fleming was named as countryman Brendon McCullum's successor in late July but did not lead the side for the recent 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to family commitments.

The 53-year-old recently flew to England for a short trip to chat with ECB officials and Test skipper Root as well as the counties, and was with the national team as they completed a 3-0 T20I whitewash under white-ball coach McCullum in Manchester on Saturday.

Image: Fleming's first assignment in charge will be the three-Test series in South Africa from December 17

Fleming - who has never been a head coach in red-ball cricket before but has extensive franchise-league experience, chiefly with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL - spoke to media ahead of the final T20I, including to Michael Atherton for the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast.

Broad said after listening to former New Zealand captain Fleming's chat with Atherton, in which he lauded Root: "What struck me was his love of leadership.

"He spoke a lot about that and strategy rather than really intricate coaching, so I am assuming he will pass a lot of the technique coaching on to his bowling coach, batting coach etc, which is what they are there to do.

'Root needs feedback Fleming will give him'

"I think what excites me is him working with Root's captaincy.

Image: Root has succeeded Ben Stokes as captain and is now in his second spell in the job after a first stint from 2017-2022

"Fleming was a good captain and has worked a lot with MS Dhoni at Chennai. He has learnt about tactical stuff on the field and how to manage changing rooms as well.

"Where Joe needs, or would like, a bit of help with his captaincy is taking a bit of weight off his shoulders at times, allowing him to just concentrate on his batting, make some tactical decisions and get feedback throughout the game to help England out.

"Joe hasn't naturally got a bowling attack that will feed back a lot of tactical advice so I think he needs that.

"As a coach you are very reliant on your captain. Fleming has had a very good one in Dhoni and maybe not quite clicked with others he tried to have success with.

"But the way he talked about Root, I imagine he will click with him."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming says the end of Bazball was 'chaotic' and that he was disappointed for outgoing captain Stokes

Broad does not view this being Fleming's first red-ball head coach role as an issue.

"He loved playing the game, he loves studying and coaching the game, so you love all formats," said the former England seamer.

"He made his name in Test match cricket and I have no doubt he has watched and been around current players."

'England need leaders to start winning Test series'

When Ben Stokes quit internationals at the end of the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer, there were few options to replace him as captain besides Root - who first led England between 2017 and 2022 - and white-ball skipper Harry Brook.

Image: England must develop leaders beyond Test skipper Root (left) and white-ball skipper Harry Brook (right)

Broad says a key part of Fleming's remit is to develop more leaders as England look to return to the peak of Test cricket, having not won any of the four five-match series they played against either Australia or India in the Bazball era.

The pundit added: "Fleming has a group that is exciting but England have also lost a lot of cricket over the last 18 months, so he has some moulding to do.

"A big problem for this team has been the lack of leaders and you can see it on the field.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming discusses his method of discipline, with England having seen a number of off-field incidents for players over the last year

"I don't really mind a lack of leaders to choose as captain when you have Root and Brook as options but on the field there has been a stark problem.

"Fleming has noticed that and will focus on that. He will drop nuggets of information in consistently throughout to try and build leadership. We need leaders to start winning Test series."

Sports.title: How to rebuild Benn & Itauma after 'mental scarring' of defeat
Sports.content:
Two big names in British boxing, earmarked as stars of the future, Moses Itauma and Conor Benn, have suffered shattering defeats in recent weeks.

Both were halted in their first world title fights. Ryan Garcia savagely ended Benn's challenge for the WBC welterweight belt in just two rounds, while Itauma crumbled in the ninth round when boxing Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF strap.

George Groves became a big name in British boxing but was no stranger to adversity in his career - it took him four attempts to win a world championship.

Captivate Captivate , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Captivate cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enablecookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Captivate cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Captivate cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

He says Itauma, who is still only 21 years old, must demonstrate his resolve.

"He's going to have to show a lot of resilience to come back from that as well as remain confident with self-belief," Groves told Sky Sports.

"There's no way you can train to that level of exhaustion. It's not like you can go into the gym and replicate that. It's never going to be, in the gym, as important as what it is - a world title fight at his age underneath the lights with everything on the line.

"He's been there now and that's a credit to him… Now you've got to use that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Toe2Toe, Delicious Orie, Barry Jones and Sam Noakes reflect on Moses Itauma's defeat to Filip Hrgovic.

"It's not an easy task but I hope that there isn't a lot of mental scarring there and they can go back and not try and reinvent. Keep what he is but just give him more comfort and confidence in the pacing of the fight."

That's something Itauma will have to learn.

"Maybe it will come with age, that endurance that he can be much more of a 12 round fighter than a three-round fighter. At the moment he's a three-round fighter. That's the sad fact of it. He's not even a six-round fighter. I thought he was gassing a bit from the third round on," Groves said.

"He's that sort of athlete, extremely fast twitch and when he punches he puts maximum effort into it. But that depletes the engine. At times he's probably never really had to work on it.

"But he's going to have to be much more efficient in his work."

Groves does think Itauma needs to regroup against an easier opponent.

"If I had to rebuild Moses Itauma. I would drop him obviously down a level but I've got to be honest I think his management has been great so far. I'm not buying into 'the Hrgovic fight was a step too far'. It was what it was. It was the right fight to make. It got elevated to a world title," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the IBF heavyweight world title fight between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic. Video credit: Courtesy of DAZN

"It was logical to elevate it to a world title and with that maybe came some pressure. Moses, he probably thought he had Hrgovic gone and he didn't and put his foot on the gas a bit too much and he gassed out. So he's going to have to own that a little bit. They'll change and adapt within his training team to patch that up.

"Get him in with someone durable, someone not as durable as Hrgovic maybe."

But Groves added: "The Hrgovic fight, it was the right fight to have.

"Hrgovic is good, he's been about, he's tough but in some ways he's made for Itauma because, although he's big and strong, he's not quick. He had nothing in that fight. The only time he has success was when Itauma just came away from his boxing style because he was exhausted," the former champion explained.

"The toughest job in boxing is probably navigating Itauma's career because he's been so good, so fast, so early, so young."

What should Benn do next?

Conor Benn also faces a tricky rebuilding job. He moved up in weight for two 160lb clashes with Chris Eubank Jr last year, worked his way back to welter for Garcia but then came unstuck.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Toe2Toe, Barry Jones reflects on Conor Benn's defeat to Ryan Garcia.

"I'm not sure where he lies at true world class," Groves said. "If he's not going to stay at 147lbs, who can he beat at 154lbs and who can he beat at 160lbs?

"I don't think [middleweight] is a good move. I'd go up to 154, I know that's a tough division with loads of really good fighters who aren't necessarily the massive marquee names.

"Maybe another camp at 147 could be good. But then you're in with Teofimo Lopez, Shakur Stevenson."

Benn will likely consider completing a trilogy with Eubank Jr, potentially at super-middleweight.

Groves said: "Hopefully it's not all roads lead to Eubank because I think that's done. That rivalry is done. I've got a feeling that's what it will be.

"I'm not a huge fan of that but that's probably the best of Conor Benn's options."

Benn has already had a number of lucrative fights. But he's not expected to call it a day there.

"He's made crazy money but I don't think he'll retire," Groves noted. "I don't think he'd want to retire off the back of that loss and he definitely won't walk away from the table when there's still food there."

Sports.title: Brown delivers Hatton tribute after winning British and Commonwealth titles
Sports.content:
Pat Brown won the vacant British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles on home turf on Saturday night, counting out John Hedges in the sixth round at Co-op Live with a body shot he dedicated to Ricky Hatton.

The 26-year-old Olympian took his professional record to seven wins from seven, every one inside the distance, adding the Lonsdale Belt to the WBA International and IBF Intercontinental titles already in his possession.

For Hedges, it was a case of unlucky number 13 after the Harlow-born fighter had gone unbeaten through his first 12 fights.

It was anything but straightforward for Brown, though. Hedges is 6ft 6in, and a southpaw, and the 24-year-old spent the opening exchanges making himself hard to hit, giving Brown nothing to aim at and grabbing hold whenever the Mancunian worked his way inside.

Frustration began to build for Brown and he started leaning on Hedges with his head and forcing him back over the top rope until referee Reece Carter intervened.

Something appeared to click in the fifth for Brown as he stopped hunting for one shot, put the jab to work and landed a right uppercut flush under the chin. Then, having aimed high for five rounds, he went to the ribs in the sixth.

A strong hook downstairs folded Hedges on to one knee and after he got to his feet, a second body shot moments later saw him downed and unable to get back up as Brown sealed an emotional and meaningful victory which he dedicated to British boxing legend Ricky Hatton, who tragically passed away a year and five days prior to the fight.

Image: Brown stopped Hedges in the sixth round (Credit: Matchroom Boxing)

Brown said: "I finished him with a body shot in memory of him."

Both fighters had strong connections to Hatton, with Brown sharing a gym with the former welterweight world champion - who also trained Hedges, taking him to the English title.

Brown was given strong support throughout from a large travelling contingent from his native Sale, with fans chanting his name from the first bell.

"I can't just go bulldozing in with him, people think you can't box," he explained on DAZN. "With John, you're not going to get him out of there straight away because he'll just make you miss and make you look silly.

"That's why it was a patient performance."

On the undercard, Shabaz Masoud shut out Ckari Mansilla 100-90 on all three cards to take the WBA International and IBF Intercontinental featherweight titles.

Elsewhere, Mark Jeffers outpointed Kieron Conway in a British super-middleweight eliminator and Cory O'Regan became English lightweight champion at the expense of Joe Howarth.

Cruz calls out Garcia after stopping Bravo

Isaac Cruz has called out Ryan Garcia after knocking out Nestor Bravo in San Diego to retain his WBC interim super-lightweight title for a second time at the Pechanga Arena in a controversial contest.

"Hey, Ryan, I'm here," Cruz, known by the nickname 'Pitbull', said after winning the fight. "My next fight for you. Come on, Ryan."

Image: Isaac Cruz won a controversial fight in San Diego

Garcia stopped Conor Benn inside two rounds in Las Vegas last Saturday to retain his WBC welterweight title.

By Monday he was talking about a fast turnaround, naming December or January for his return and Cruz among the men he would face.

Whether it is that simple is another matter as Garcia has also been linked with a fight against Teofimo Lopez, who holds a world title at welterweight, while Cruz operates a division below.

Garcia responded to callout following the fight, though, and said: "Pitbull proved me wrong tonight. Let's do this in December, the offer is on the table.

Image: Ryan Garcia with Conor Benn after their contest in Las Vegas

"I can tame a lion, I'm not to concerned about taming a pitbull."

On Saturday night though, Cruz boxed effectively and started fast as he caught Bravo with a hook in the first round as the Puerto Rican attempted to tie up.

Then came the controversy, courtesy of the referee.

Thomas Taylor took a point off Bravo in the second for holding, warned both men in the third after a series of low blows and docked the Puerto Rican again in the fourth for dumping Cruz on the canvas - telling him bluntly that a disqualification would leave him unpaid.

The fight ended in the sixth as a lead left hook landed clean midway through the round, knocking Bravo to the canvas as he lost for just the second time in his career, while Cruz moves to 29-3-2.

Daniel Blancas, Marco Verde and Eumir Marcial all won inside the distance on the undercard.

Sports.title: Fleming wants England back top of Test rankings as 'work to be done' on discipline
Sports.content:
New England Test head coach Stephen Fleming has spoken of his desire to return the team to the top of the world rankings, adding that there is "work to be done" on the side's disciplinary issues that have dominated headlines this summer.

In June, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended from the second Test of the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand due to a nightclub incident that occurred in the wake of their opening win at Lord's.

Last month, Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series whitewash of Pakistan, prompting Test captain Joe Root to describe himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

Carse did not face any charges after police closed their investigation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look back at an extraordinary summer of Test series which saw Ben Stokes retire, a new England captain, the end of Bazball, and a series sweep of Pakistan

"It's disappointing," Fleming said. "The way that players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me."

He added: "I watched Joe in the press conference, and when he voices his displeasure at the behaviour, I think that said it all.

"If you want a great example of how to behave as an international cricketer, Joe Root is it.

"There's work to be done, and that comes back to making sure we're tying into something a bit bigger than oneself."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming discusses his method of discipline, with England having seen a number of off-field incidents for players over the last year

As well as having "a lot of contact" with Root since accepting the Test job on July 30 and throughout the Pakistan series - which Fleming was not yet in post for, due to family and commercial commitments - the new coach said he had also been in touch with Stokes, who retired from international cricket in June.

Amid suggestions of a possible return for the home Ashes series next summer, Fleming said of the 35-year-old: "He's really happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision.

"My view is that when a player decides to retire, it's a big decision, and I have the utmost respect for that decision."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes reflects on his decision to retire from international cricket and explains why it was the right time

Fleming excited for Ashes and keen to take England to top

Fleming admitted he is already excited about coaching England in next summer's Ashes, calling it "an absolute highlight", while he also talked up the potential of the team he is about to take over.

"I would love to be in charge of the number one Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration," Fleming said.

"My honest appraisal is it's a great time to be the head coach. I think it's a real opportunity with the players that are coming through.

It's one of the most prestigious jobs in cricket, and I was very honoured to be asked... The opportunity to take up this role is one that you don't turn down.

"The fast bowlers as an example, I loved watching them operate in the [Pakistan] Test series recently.

"Also, the introduction of [Jordan] Cox and [Dan] Lawrence was nice, when you've got someone like [Jacob] Bethell [to come back].

"There's talent there competing for places, and that's always the barometer. If you're leaving very good players out, then you're going to be in a healthy situation."

Image: Jordan Cox (left) and Dan Lawrence (right) impressed during the Pakistan Test series

Fleming added on the World Test Championship, in which England sit sixth in the 2025-2027 cycle - having failed to reach the final of any of the previous three editions: "I think England could do much better in that.

"If that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it, along with every other marquee event that comes our way?

"That opportunity is real, but there's a huge amount of work to do."

Fleming rejects 'Flemball' in pursuit of 'cricket sense'

As for the playing style Fleming will look for his team to adopt, he was keen to praise the prior work of Stokes and former New Zealand team-mate - England's current white-ball coach - Brendon McCullum, but said he is looking to "combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fleming says the end of Bazball was 'chaotic' and that he was disappointed for outgoing captain Stokes

There will be no 'Bazball' style moniker to accompany his team's style, however, as per his predecessor.

"That's a medical condition," Fleming joked when presented with the prospect of 'Flemball'.

"The way they [Stokes and McCullum] changed the nature of Test cricket was quite remarkable, and I have a huge amount of respect for the courage that that took.

"Obviously, the last 12 months it hasn't evolved as they would have liked and the fans would have liked, but I still acknowledge that period of two years [prior]."

He added: "I really loved the positive play and the freeing up of the England players, so if I could take that and combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments.

"There are key times in a match that you have to be really smart, and maybe we can just work a bit harder on that - but still combine positive nature of the players that are in there."

Root is 'greatness' and 'the best guy to captain Test team'

Talking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Fleming elaborated further on the respect he has for Root and how delighted he is to have him as captain of the Test team.

Root had previously captained England from 2017-2022 before being replaced by Stokes following a barren run of one win in his last 17 Tests.

Upon Stokes' resignation, white-ball skipper Harry Brook could have been an all-format option, but Fleming is thrilled that Root accepted the role again.

"I am a really big fan of Root," Fleming said. "I think he is a wonderful player and ambassador for the game, so to work with him was really appealing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root hailed England's adaptability with the bat and his high-quality bowling attack after the team stormed to a Test series win over Pakistan in his first series back as captain

"I just knew that he is the best guy to captain this side. He epitomises everything that is great about an international player. He is greatness, but a wonderful human being in the way that he conducts himself and can go about being great.

"He is such a great role model and such a perfect person for a young group of players. It was a no-brainer, for me, for him to be captain.

"Root is in charge. If he is going out and making key decisions, he is in charge. My role is very closely linked to provide him with what he needs. That can be criticism, constructively, so it's not just a yes position.

"I want him to be the best he can be and I think there is still room to grow in his captaincy with this group. I don't necessarily know what that looks like but I know there is growth and that's exciting."
