Sports.title: What's happening with JJ Gabriel? Man Utd bombshell, Barcelona flight, Carrick comments
Sports.content:
What's happening with JJ Gabriel? Man Utd bombshell, Barcelona flight, Carrick comments

JJ Gabriel's request for Manchester United to de-register him rocked the club this week as the 15-year-old phenom continues to seek an exit

View 5 Images JJ Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Manchester United are still reeling from JJ Gabriel's shock request to leave. But where exactly do things stand?

‌



On September 15, news broke that Gabriel, one of United's most promising young players and perhaps one of the Premier League's brightest prospects, wanted to have his youth registration terminated.

‌



This request stunned the club and came the day before they faced Brighton in the Carabao Cup. It was expected that Gabriel, who could have become United's youngest-ever player if he'd made an appearance, would at least be in the matchday squad. The tie was lost 3-2 and Gabriel was omitted. He has not trained since.

‌



While United feel the situation can be repaired, the youngster looks set for an exit and has flown to Barcelona as rumours swirl that Gabriel wishes to join another European giant. Mirror Football takes a look at where things stand.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

JJ Gabriel snubbed for England youth call-ups days after Man Utd star demanded to quit READ MORE :

Initial bombshell

Because Gabriel is only 15, his request, which shook United, was for his de-registration. He cannot sign a professional contract until he is 17 or a scholarship agreement until he turns 16 on October 6.

‌



View 5 Images The teenager's request to have his registration cancelled was denied (Image: Getty)

Therefore, the only thing currently tying him to United is a Premier League youth registration. However, for this to be cancelled, all parties must agree. This means that the club, the player and the player's parent/guardian must all give consent.

Of course, Gabriel's request made it clear that he and his guardian would agree, but United did not. Had they opted to say yes, then Gabriel would have become a free agent with immediate effect.

‌



Reports suggested that Gabriel's initial disgruntlement, one of the primary reasons the request was submitted, stemmed from broken promises of senior involvement. This is not the first time United have faced a battle for Gabriel either. In 2025, executive director Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada had to intervene to stop him from joining Manchester City.

Barcelona journey

However, despite United rejecting his initial request, Gabriel has made it clear that, as things stand, he wants to leave. He has even gone as far as travelling to Barcelona to hear a pitch from the Catalan giants.

View 5 Images Gabriel flew to Barcelona (Image: Getty)

‌



It is not just La Blaugrana who are supposedly interested, with Real Madrid and other major European powerhouses also being mooted. It is understood that he first travelled to France and then to Spain, where meetings were concluded.

Gabriel remains registered at United's academy after they rejected his demand, but this might not stop him from leaving. Because he can obtain a European Union passport through either his former Republic of Ireland international father or mother, who has Greek-Cypriot heritage, once he turns 16, he could refuse a scholarship offer and sign directly with a continental club.

Under Premier League rules, turning 16 does not automatically grant him free agency or allow him to sign with another English side. Because United maintain his domestic academy registration, he could not simply head for Chelsea or Arsenal without the club's agreement or a tribunal settlement.

‌



View 5 Images The 15-year-old has trained with the first team for some time (Image: Getty)

But this doesn't apply to clubs in mainland Europe. Whilst FIFA rules normally prevent UK-based teenagers from moving to EU sides until they turn 18 post-Brexit, obtaining an EU passport unlocks the FIFA Article 19 EU exception. Because Gabriel qualifies for EU citizenship through his family, securing those documents will allow him to sign directly with a continental team once he turns 16.

Gabriel will celebrate his next birthday on October 6 and when he does, United could do nothing to stop him from jetting off to Barcelona or Real Madrid, for example, and exploiting this loophole. They'd only be entitled to standard FIFA training compensation of around £300,000.

‌



Michael Carrick's comments

United boss Michael Carrick kept a level head when asked about Gabriel on Tuesday evening. He stressed that the situation involves such a young player and mustn't be taken out of proportion.

"We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy," said Carrick. "It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child, really. He's certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure and how much we jump on that."

View 5 Images Carrick played down the situation after the Brighton defeat (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

When he was asked if he was involved in the discussions around the player's future, Carrick added: "As a club, for sure, we're all involved in those conversations. I just think we've got to be very careful of that."

As things stand, though, his club have denied an immediate termination of his registration, but it appears Gabriel is set for an acrimonious departure. United still believe the situation can be mended.

But reports in Spain suggest Gabriel could obtain the necessary documentation to eventually move abroad as early as next week. Everything will fall into place when he celebrates his 16th birthday, which is just over two weeks away.

Sports.title: BBC Sport staff eye strike action amid split on restructure plans and redundancies
Sports.content:
BBC Sport staff eye strike action amid split on restructure plans and redundancies

BBC Sport are eyeing up more changes ahead of a potential restructure, leading to more changes, as some staff consider strike action

View 2 Images BBC's Sport department are making more changes, which has led to some backlash (Image: 2024 James Gill - Danehouse)

BBC Sport staff are considering strike action after the announcement of more redundancies and a planned restructure.

‌



Director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski will speak next week with the expectation being the planned changes will result in several job losses. Existing employees will be offered voluntary redundancy as the department continue with its desire to modernise, reports the Daily Mail.

‌



But in response some staff are considering going on strike with the newsroom very much split on whether the organisation at MediaCity is going in the right direction.

‌



Some believe that Kay-Jelski is going too far with his desire to seek a younger, digital-focussed audience, but others claim that the changes have been long overdue.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Kay-Jelski has already presided over mass changes within BBC Sport and last year sanctioned dozens of redundancies. Recently the organisation announced it was binning Ski Sunday. Other events have been dropped, including the Commonwealth Games, the Boat Race and the Rugby League World Cup.

At the end of last season, long-running show Football Focus was axed, bringing down the curtain on 52 years of coverage. At the time Kay-Jelski denied that the move had come about as a result of cost-cutting.

BBC Sport's coverage of the World Cup was also heavily criticised with the corporation choosing to conduct its coverage from its Salford base, only sending a cluster of pundits and reporters out for the tournament. Meanwhile rivals ITV boasted a stunning studio in New York, overlooking the Manhattan skyline.

‌



View 2 Images BBC director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski is determined to attract a younger audience

Gary Lineker, one of the BBC's most recognisable faces for decades, recently left the company and has started up his own venture. He has since expressed his affection for the BBC, but didn't shy away from admitting its faults.

He said on Davina McCall's Begin Again podcast: "I will say that I love the BBC for all its faults. I mean, and it has a few. But it's an amazing institution, and it's hugely respected around the world, and we should be proud of it."

Article continues below

He did add: "But yet, I must say though, living life outside of the BBC without having that thing on show, it's nice not treading on eggshells all the time."

Sports.title: Former Premier League player immediately resigns as manager in shock post-match interview
Sports.content:
Former Premier League player immediately resigns as manager in shock post-match interview

Former Premier League star Lee Clark has quit as Hartlepool boss in a stunning post-match interview, where he announced his resignation after fan backlash and poor results

View 2 Images Lee Clark has quit as Hartlepool boss

Former Newcastle and Fulham star Lee Clark resigned as Hartlepool boss immediately after their loss to Worthing, announcing his decision to quit in the post-match interview.

‌



Clark only took over at Victoria Park in the summer after a short spell with Rotherham last season, but he's overseen a poor run of results, which culminated with a home loss that saw him make the decision to walk away.

‌



Hartlepool have lost six of their last seven games, which has seen them tumble down the table and they now sit 19th, despite having ambitions to end their spell in non-league. Fans called for Clark's head during Saturday's game and the former top flight pro has now walked away.

‌



He told BBC Radio Tees: "I resign from my position with immediate effect. I wanted to give this club and the fans something to be proud of, what they deserve, but I haven't been able to do that unfortunately."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Clark added: "I was excited to take the job and I wanted to be the man to get them back to where they need to be and deserve to be, but it hasn't worked out."

Hartlepool were taken over in January by American businessman Landon Smith with the club looking to return to the Football League for the first time in four years. However the bombshell news means they will look their ninth permanent boss since entering non-league.

Since 2024 no manager has taken charge of more than 34 games before being dismissed. Among those are former Sunderland striker Kevin Phillips, who got 16 games, and ex-Leeds boss Simon Grayson, who lasted 15 matches.

‌



View 2 Images He leaves with Hartlepool 19th in the National League

Clark previously made history as a manager when he was in charge of Huddersfield Town. He led the Terriers to a record 43 league games without defeat, surpassing the record held by Nottingham Forest. It was a period that spanned 11 months when they were in League One

He's since taken charge of Birmingham, Blackpool and Kilmarnock whilst also having a period in the Middle East.

Article continues below

As a player Clark made 240 appearances for Newcastle during the 1990s before ending up at Fulham, via Sunderland. Whilst in west London he scored in a 3-1 win against Manchester United, Fulham's first win at Old Trafford in 39 years.

Sports.title: Richarlison takes to social media with clear message after Tottenham lose again
Sports.content:
Richarlison takes to social media with clear message after Tottenham lose again

Richarlison has been left out of the Tottenham squad for the Premier League this season and the forward posted on social media after their latest defeat

View 2 Images Richarlison has posted two messages on social media (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur striker Richarlison posted two messages on social media just a few hours after the club were beaten in the Premier League. Spurs were on the receiving end of a 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon, leaving the club still without a win going into the international break.

‌



Richarlison posted two messages on Instagram on Saturday, with the first being a video of himself in training, accompanied by the caption, “The focus remains”.

‌



The Brazilian’s second post was another video, this time doing some sprint training, which included the caption, "35.4km/h - I broke my record”.

‌



The messages from Richarlison came just a few hours after Tottenham’s defeat in north London, with Spurs now picking up just two points from their opening five Premier League matches.

Ex-Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior clashes with former players after gesture to fans READ MORE :

Unai Emery's men emerged 3-2 victors against Roberto De Zerbi's team, having established a three-goal cushion before Conor Gallagher sparked a late comeback in the 86th minute, while Jan Paul van Hecke netted a consolation strike during stoppage time.

De Zerbi has made his position crystal clear that Richarlison will not play for the club following his public desire to depart north London during the summer transfer window.

‌



The striker did not feature in Tottenham's Carabao Cup loss to Liverpool and has not been included in their 25-man squad for the Premier League.

"Richarlison, you already know everything and nothing change for Carabao Cup or Premier League. The situation is the same," De Zerbi said.

‌

"I stay in the middle and I can't say nothing more because it is not my job. I can answer about the result and the players in the squad, the offensive phase, the defensive phase, but not for other things.

"What I have done at the beginning of this season has been to speak with him and to propose an extension of the contract. If he said, 'no thank you,' I finished my job.

"I stay within the club. It's coach and club together. At the start of this season I spoke to him many times to convince him to stay and he didn't want to. I can't go every day to pray for him to stay."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick fronts up on Pro Ref's apology after Manchester derby error
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick fronts up on Pro Ref's apology after Manchester derby error

Michael Carrick admits the apology from Pro Ref for last weekend's VAR howler in the Manchester derby didn't mean anything, but remains a believer in the technology

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has brushed off the apology given by Pro Ref

Michael Carrick admits that receiving an apology from Pro Ref for the VAR error that cost Manchester United last weekend's Manchester derby "doesn't mean an awful lot"

‌



Howard Webb, the head of Pro Ref, admitted the error after Erling Haaland’s winning strike was allowed to stand despite Manchester City team-mate Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position, which was overlooked by the officials at the time.

‌



Haaland's goal was originally chalked off before a VAR review reversed the on-field decision. It was apparent at the time that those operating VAR may have made an error and an apology arrived shortly after full-time.

‌



VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus have been stood down in light of the incident, which has again ignited the debate over the system. But Carrick insists he remains a believer in the technology, but the apology for last week didn't particularly resonate.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said: "Listen, one-off things can happen. At the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don't think I need to go over that. Yes, I've got faith in it, of course. It’s the system that we work towards and that we use, so the apology doesn't mean an awful lot.

"I can appreciate it and I respect them for putting their hands up and saying 'we got that wrong”' It happens. Moving forward, we just have to deal with what's thrown in front of us. Maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out; percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be."

The loss was damning as it left United with four points from their opening four games, and since then they've made unwanted history by letting a 2-0 lead slip at Old Trafford as Brighton secured a 3-2 success in Manchester.

‌



View 2 Images Erling Haaland's winning goal was given despite Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position (Image: Getty Images)

That defeat has seen Carrick field questions on his future this week, speculation he labelled "ridiculous", but he has urged his side to put the setback behind them with United needing to snap their losing streak.

"That was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game, and that's why it was particularly tough," he said. "It can have an impact in that moment of time – it can have a big impact – but we can't let it have an impact on the rest of the season. That's for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible."

Sports.title: 'I moved to Fulham from Man Utd and it was the best decision I made because of Red Devils boss'
Sports.content:
'I moved to Fulham from Man Utd and it was the best decision I made because of Red Devils boss'

The former Manchester United star utilised a unique method to engineer his Old Trafford exit

View 2 Images The former Manchester United star was determined to leave the club (Image: getty images)

Determined to leave Manchester United on his own terms, Andreas Pereira actively avoided speaking with incoming manager Erik ten Hag to ensure nothing derailed his exit. The Brazilian midfielder departed the Red Devils in 2022 to join Fulham in a £10million deal to end his 11-year association with the club.

‌



His two former clubs meet at Craven Cottage today (Sunday, September 20) and Pereira knew from their shared history at PSV Eindhoven how persuasive Ten Hag could be. After making 75 appearances for United alongside loan spells at Granada, Valencia, Lazio, and current side Flamengo, the 30-year-old knew he needed a clean break rather than another fight for first-team minutes at Old Trafford.

‌



"I didn't speak with Ten Hag," Pereira told ESPN during his first season at Fulham. "I know him because I worked with him at PSV but I was determined in my head and maybe if I spoke with the manager again I would stay.

‌



"In my head I was thinking 'I need to go, I need to feel confident and play' and that's what I did. At United I had a lot of memories; good memories, bad memories. It's been 10 years at the club. I arrived when I was 16 so, you know, a young boy. It was an amazing ride but I got to the stage where I thought maybe it was best not to stay.

"I wanted to feel more loved and I wanted to play every game. What Fulham offered me and what [manager] Marco [Silva] offered me, it was the perfect opportunity." Pereira enjoyed his most successful spell in west London, netting 10 goals across 119 appearances for the Cottagers.

‌

He confessed that departing Manchester was the finest decision he'd ever taken and held no remorse about leaving the club. "I think it was the best decision I made in my life," Pereira told the Evening Standard in 2024.

"To come to live and play here, to enjoy my football, to get back into the national team with great players, to enjoy my football in the Premier League, leaving is the best decision I made. The time I was there, I really enjoyed being at a fantastic club. But I don't regret leaving.

View 2 Images Andreas Pereira got his start in United's first team under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (Image: getty images)

‌



"We [the players in my situation] have this desire to show it was wrong that we didn't play. With everyone's help around me [at Fulham], I achieved a great season. [Marco Silva] is responsible for me coming to Fulham. I will always be grateful for everything he has done for me."

Sunday's clash between the two sides follows United's stunning Carabao Cup elimination on Wednesday. United surrendered a 2-0 lead at home to Brighton, who fought back to triumph 3-2 and advance to the fourth round.

Sports.title: 'Michael Carrick sack talk is nonsense – Man Utd's players simply aren't doing enough'
Sports.content:
'Michael Carrick sack talk is nonsense – Man Utd's players simply aren't doing enough'

Back-to-back defeats have prompted questions about the future of Manchester United manager Michael Carrick but not everyone is convinced

View 2 Images Michael Carrick will want a response from his players against Fulham on Sunday (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Former Manchester United defender Phil Bardsley has played down suggestions manager Michael Carrick should be worried for his future. Instead, he has called on the players to step up and help recover from a tough start to the season.

‌



United, who face Fulham on Sunday, have earned just four points from their first four league matches despite facing only one team who finished in the top half of the table last season. They got off to a winning start in Europe, beating Sabah 4-0, but are out of the Carabao Cup after surrendering a 2-0 lead to lose at home to Brighton.

‌



Back-to-back defeats against Manchester City in the league and Brighton in the cup have seen questions asked about what's next for Carrick, who only took the job on a permanent basis in the close-season. However, academy graduate Bardsley rubbished talk of a change in the dugout.

‌



"I think that's a lot of nonsense," the Scotland international told Lyllo Casino. "That's a lot of outside noise, and it's always the way if you look at certain top clubs losing games or going on a bit of a losing run. It's never as big as when Man United go on a bit of a difficult losing streak.

Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question READ MORE :

Barcelona star reveals how Marcus Rashford got reality check before Man Utd return READ MORE :

He continued: "So it is what it is, it's the magnitude of the club. You're always going to get criticism, and if you're not prepared to take the criticism, then you're at the wrong club because there's going to be highs and lows at that club, and it's how you bounce back.

‌



"But as a collective, the players are just not doing enough for me. We can go back to say managers, Mourinho, Van Gaal, Amorim, Carrick, all these brilliant coaches.

"But the stoppage is with the players, and there's got to be some demand on each other to start getting results. Ultimately, it is what it is, and they find themselves where they are. It's the players that have got to dig themselves out of this little bit of a tricky situation."

View 2 Images Brighton ended United's Carabao Cup run on Wednesday (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Carrick has given minutes to new signings Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow already this season but £70m arrival Carlos Baleba is still waiting for his United debut. Speaking ahead of Sunday's meeting with Fulham, the manager indicated the Cameroon international is getting closer to a debut for his new club.

"We're looking good. Everyone's up and running Over the last week or so, pretty much everyone has played and [been] fit and we're trying to get Carlos back in," Carrick told club media.

"Well, I say back in, actually introducing him into the group. So he's done a bit of training this week and, hopefully, we'll get Luke [Shaw] back in and around it this week and look forward to a strong game on the weekend."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
