He said he wanted to "address the question of where I stand in the situation in Israel and Palestine, and whether my doing this concert here tonight implies where I stand".

"I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind, because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division", he continued. "But this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore."

Sheeran said what happened in Israel on 7 October was "horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain", and what was happening in Gaza was "catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate".

"My heart has been broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilian lives, of children's lives, and this systemic injustice we're seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked."

He said he was working out how to contribute in a way that would help "victims of these terrible times - and listening and learning, because I do not know enough".

World.title: German elections under way which could decide fate of Chancellor Merz
World.content:
Local elections are taking place in two German states on Sunday which could increase the political pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

Opinion polls in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommerm suggest Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) is at risk of damaging defeats, which would raise further questions about the chancellor's future.

These latest elections come after the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won a major victory in the state of Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago, while the CDU saw its vote halved.

There has been speculation in Germany that Merz could be replaced as chancellor mid-term unless the CDU's political fortunes improve.

He has said he will carry on but is facing poor approval ratings amid rumours of a so-called chancellor swap, though his challengers are "still hesitating", writes German news site Tagesschau, external.

According to the polls, Merz's conservatives could lose power in Berlin as it tussles with Die Linke (The Left) over first place.

Meanwhile in the north-eastern state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the CDU has only just been hovering above the 5% threshold needed for a party to enter the state parliament. It could spell their worst ever result in a state election.

World.title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi capital with ballistic missiles
World.content:
Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen say they carried out drone and ballistic missile attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh, as well as energy sites on the country's Red Sea coast.

Saudi authorities said they intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh on Saturday, without confirming any further strikes or causalities.

Earlier, a column of black smoke was seen rising from fuel tanks near the Saudi capital's international airport, where flights were disrupted temporarily on Saturday.

Air raid alerts had sounded in the capital for the first time since the Iran-backed Houthis increased their attacks on Saudi Arabia in July.

The US state department urged Americans in the Middle East to "exercise vigilance and be prepared for potential flight cancellations and other travel disruptions".

"Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly," it said in a statement.

It added that Americans "should seriously reconsider travel to and through the region".

Air defences also stopped "hostile attempts to target civilians" in the cities of Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu, an official spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said in a statement.

In a statement posted online, Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said a "large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones" had been used to attack "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and Aramco state oil and gas company facilities in Yanbu on the coast.

He added that the attacks were "in response to the Saudi enemy's criminal attempts" to target the Yemeni capital Sanaa, which is currently controlled by the Houthis.

Earlier, Sarea had accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out 300 strikes across Yemen during the past week.

The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.

They have attacked targets inside Saudi Arabia on several occasions in recent months, and said this week that they were responsible for downing a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen.

According to an unconfirmed report from AFP news agency, quoting military sources on both sides of Yemen's civil war, fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces claimed 48 lives on Saturday.

The Houthis said 31 of their fighters had been killed while government sources said their side had lost 17 soldiers, according to the news agency.

On Friday, the International Organization for Migration, a UN body, reported that the number of people displaced as a result of recent fighting had passed 104,796, external.

World.title: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
World.content:
The US and Denmark have announced a deal on Greenland's security, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump's threats to seize it by force.

Nato said the deal would help stabilise the region, as Trump said Denmark would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory in the Arctic.

The leaders of Denmark and Greenland welcomed the deal to "strengthen security", saying it was expected to be signed next week - but did not outline its contents.

This comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns, citing its strategic location for defence purposes and its mineral wealth.

No text of the agreement has been released. Trump said the deal came with "no cost to the United States" and would grant it the ability "to do what is necessary" to "secure and defend the security of Greenland", in a post on Truth Social.

He said it included a rule that no US adversary could maintain a military presence in Greenland or "make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval".

A Nato spokesperson said the military alliance welcomed the deal, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.

The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.

The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.

Nielsen said it was "gratifying that we are about to enter into an agreement that ensures and strengthens the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States and the Western alliance".

"The agreement recognises Greenland's interests and our place in international co-operation. It is for the benefit of us all," he said.

Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron said the deal helped "to reaffirm Danish sovereignty" over the island.

"I simply note that Danish sovereignty is respected, that international law is respected, and that this is what we were asking for. So it's a good thing," Macron was quoted as saying by the AFP news agency.

World.title: Our head teacher was an abuser. We joined forces to get justice - now we're married
World.content:
Sukma, for her part, told us she was called to Abah's house to discover two police officers and an NWDI lawyer waiting for her. They forced her to sign a document saying all her allegations were lies, she said. Her account is backed up by a secret recording she later made as she challenged Abah's wife, Hurmiati.

Hurmiati can be heard telling her to respect their "agreement" that nothing happened, adding: "Do you want this to haunt you for the rest of your life? Do you want it to damage the chances of you getting married?"

This pressure even extended to Abah asking Yusron's parents to fly to Jakarta to look for him at university. They didn't find him - he was hiding in a hotel - but the ordeal was too much for Yusron's mother. She told her son the stress was killing her.

So Yusron reluctantly stopped his investigation.

Meanwhile he and Zia were slowly getting closer. The friendship had become a long-distance relationship, and they were regularly speaking on the phone.

"And I could see she was really strugglingâ¦ She'd say things like: 'Why do I keep thinking about what [Abah] did?'."

Yusron was torn between helping the girl he was falling in love with, and the promise he had made to his mother.

And then, eight months later, Yusron heard about a group raising awareness about sexual abuse in Islamic schools. It had been set up by a young woman called Ayu Masruroh, who had helped her friend get justice after she had been sexually assaulted at another school, by a teacher called Moch Subchi Azal Tsani.

Ayu was now actively posting on social media about the need to speak out.

It inspired Zia to post a call-out on Instagram, asking any Indonesian student who had experienced abuse to get in touch.

And she was to discover that, despite Abah's remonstrations, and promises to change, he had apparently offended again. Someone who went to Zia's school got in touch to say she too had been sexually exploited by Abah. The alleged abuse had taken place almost a year after his pledges to Zia and Yusron.

"It made me realise [Abah] hadn't really changed at allâ¦ all the things he said about stoppingâ¦ It was all just lies," said Zia.

If you are in the UK, and have been affected by issues of sexual abuse or violence, information and support is available at BBC Action Line

Yusron's parents finally agreed he should help Zia and Sukma to continue their quest for justice.

But this time, the friends decided to do things differently. They contacted Ayu, and she was clear: get a lawyer. She introduced them to someone experienced in representing sexual abuse survivors. He advised that Sukma's case was the strongest to ensure a prosecution.

We contacted Abah and Hurmiati about the allegations against them - they did not respond.

NWDI said it was still investigating the allegations internally and denied ever trying to cover up sexual abuse claims.

It said it had "a duty to safeguard the organisation from being tarnished by the alleged actions of individuals".

Sukma filed her claim against Abah to the police in February last year. She is still waiting for them to take action and Abah is still in post.

"I don't want what happened to me, to happen to any other students. I want justice," she told the BBC.

The investigation has, however, brought Zia and Yusron ever closer. Last February, after three years of messaging and speaking, Yusron decided to move to Cairo to be with her.

World.title: Cultural treasures are being destroyed worldwide - so why is no-one being punished?
World.content:
August was a brutal month for Ukraine. Russian aerial attacks increased significantly, launching thousands of drones. Kyiv was intensely bombarded, as were the southern cities of Mykolaiv and Odesa. Amid the destruction and loss of life, Odesa reported damage to six Unesco-protected sites, including the salmon-pink 19th Century Alexandru Sturdza House.

It raised again the question of why it is so hard to hold actors accountable for the destruction of buildings and objects with real cultural significance.

In the last month alone, Ukraine's Ministry of Culture reported that 148 cultural heritage sites were recorded as damaged or destroyed, including in Odesa.

Several Ukrainian activist groups have tried to get accountability by lodging complaints with the International Criminal Court (ICC) against Russia over cultural destruction and looting, but no indictments have been issued.

Bijan Rouhani, a senior researcher at the Endangered Archaeology in the Middle East and North Africa project, says that the legal framework may be strong on paper but in practice it almost inevitably falls short. "No state actor has ever been tried for this offence. The obstacle is no longer evidence. We have satellite imagery, remote sensing and monitoring teams. The obstacle is jurisdiction and political will."

Looking at the cauldron of conflicts convulsing the world, the question is ever more pressing as to whether effective action is possible to stop the damage being done or ensure accountability when it does.

World.title: Journalists denied White House access after Trump banned some media outlets
World.content:
Politico, CNN and MS NOW journalists have been denied access to the White House after US President Donald Trump announced he was banning the outlets.

An MS NOW reporter and a photographer tried entering the White House grounds on Saturday morning, but their badges would not scan and an officer confiscated them, the outlet reported.

Both CNN and Politico also said Saturday morning that their reporters were denied access and had their badges seized.

Trump said on Friday he was barring all three major US media outlets from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.

"The officer asked me to hand over my badge. He said that it was disabled," MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner said. "I asked why I was not able to get inside. He said it was above him."

Gardner added that while her and her colleague's badges were disabled, an MS NOW producer was still able to scan her badge to get in, though she was not given an explanation as to why the producer's badge still worked.

CNN reporter Betsy Klein said a Secret Service agent told her her badge had been deactivated.

World.title: APC’s Kallamu wins Gombe/Kwami /Funakaye Federal Constituency by-election – Official
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Usman Kallamu, has won the Gombe/Kwami/Funakaye Federal Constituency by-election held on Saturday in Gombe State.

The result was announced on Sunday by Umar Gurama of the Federal University of Kashere, who served as the returning officer for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The announcement took place at the Malam-Sidi collation centre in the Kwami Local Government Area.

Mr Gurama, a professor, said Mr Kallamu polled 41,121 votes to defeat candidates of the Labour Party (LP), All Progressives Movement (APM) and New Nigeria Peoples Party (NDP).

The LP candidate scored 3,553 votes, while APM and NDP candidates polled 872 and 707 votes, respectively.

“With his 41,121 votes, Kallamu secured the highest number of votes to emerge winner of the bye-election,” he said.

Mr Gurama said a total of 47,301 votes were cast in the election, out of which 46,551 were declared valid, while 750 votes were rejected.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The by-election was conducted to fill the vacant seat in the House of Representatives following the death of the former representative of the constituency, Yaya Bauchi -Tongo.

The election was conducted across 903 polling units in 31 Registration Areas covering Gombe, Kwami and Funakaye Local Government Areas.

World.title: NDLEA intercepts N3.4bn loud, opioids, arrests fake police officer, mechanic-drug dealer
World.content:
Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) have intercepted more than 1.3 million pills of tramadol and other opioids, as well as 6,000 kilograms of potent strains of cannabis, with a combined street value of more than N3.4 billion.

NDLEA’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, said in a statement on Sunday in Abuja that the breakthroughs were achieved in a string of major operations across Lagos, Edo, Niger, Delta, Ondo, Gombe, Imo and the FCT.

Mr Babafemi said that at the top of the line-up of successful operations was the interception of 1,200 parcels of Canadian Loud, a synthetic strain of cannabis.

He said that the drug was with a gross weight of 603.75 kilograms and valued at N1.8billion.

He also said that NDLEA operatives arrested an alleged trafficker who impersonated a senior police officer to evade scrutiny at checkpoints while ferrying drugs across state lines.

Mr Babafemi added that the 49-year-old fake police officer was arrested on Wednesday, 16 Sept by NDLEA operatives along the Benin-Onitsha expressway in Asaba, Delta.

He also added that the suspect was in possession of 292.48 kilograms of skunk hidden in his silver Toyota Sienna bus.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Investigation established that the suspect had long paraded himself as Godwin Emeka, a Deputy Superintendent of Police, using a forged ID card to escape scrutiny at checkpoints while transporting illicit consignments.

“An accomplice, a 39-year-old man, was arrested along with him,” he said.

Meanwhile, in Edo, NDLEA operatives acting on intelligence stormed a location on Agbor Road, Benin City, where they arrested a 45-year-old man who used his auto-repair workshop as a front for storing illicit drugs.

Mr Babafemi said that officers recovered 48 kilograms of Canadian Loud and 152 grams of methamphetamine, along with a metal box used to store the illicit substances.

At the Tin-Can Island Port in Lagos, a 40-foot container shipped from Montreal, Canada, and arrived on 12 September, was placed under intensive monitoring by NDLEA operatives based on processed intelligence.

Mr Babafemi said that the shipment was eventually subjected to a full joint physical examination with Customs and other security agencies on Wednesday, Sept. 16.

“The search uncovered 1,200 parcels of Canadian Loud weighing 603.75 kilograms, concealed inside 31 black jumbo bags loaded within two Toyota Sienna vehicles in the container,” he said.

He further said that NDLEA operatives in Niger, while on patrol along the Abuja-Kaduna expressway at Chachi, Tafa Local Government Area, on Tuesday, Sept. 15, arrested three young suspects.

Mr Babafemi said that the suspects were with two locally fabricated AK-47 rifles and a magazine, a locally made pistol with a magazine, and nine rounds of 9mm ammunition concealed in a black travel bag.

He added that the agency’s operatives similarly arrested two suspects on Friday, 18 Sept., along the Abaji-Abuja highway.

Over 1.1 million assorted tramadol tablets/capsules, codeine syrup, methamphetamine and Exol tablets concealed in eight sacks en route from Onitsha, Anambra state, to Mararaba, Nasarawa state, were recovered from them.

” In another development, in Lagos, a suspected drug dealer was arrested on Friday, Sept. 18, at his residence in Aguda, Surulere, with 48,900 pills of tramadol 225mg.

“Also, seven cartons of cannabis sativa weighing 59kg were intercepted at a logistics company with a suspect taken into custody,” he said.

In another operation in Lagos, Babafemi said that another suspected drug peddler was arrested at Apongbo with 998.38kg of nitrous oxide gas on Thursday, Sept.17.

“Additionally, a total of 154,480 capsules of tramadol were recovered from two suspects who were arrested at the Barunde area and the Gombe main market, respectively, in Gombe state on Friday, Sept. 18.

“However, a suspect was also arrested along the Owerri-Onitsha road, Imo state, with 43.85kg of skunk on Friday, Sept. 18.

Four suspects were nabbed during a raid and the destruction of 5,000 kilograms of skunk on a two-hectare cannabis farm in Ita-Ogbolu forest, Ondo state, on Tuesday, Sept. 15.

“No less than 48kg of dry and fresh cannabis was recovered from the location for the prosecution of the suspects,” he said.

With the same vigour, Babafemi said that commands and formations of the agency across the country continued their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation activities.

This, he said, was taken to schools, worship centres, workplaces, and communities, among others, in the past week.

READ ALSO: Lagos APC orders candidates to stay in Nigeria until 2027 polls

“The places include: WADA enlightenment lecture to students and staff of St. Ferdinand School, Ogbomoso, Oyo; Unizik Secondary School, Awka, Anambra; Scholars Nursery and Primary School, Epe, Lagos, and Government Technical Training School, Jalingo, Taraba state.

“The Delta Ports Command of NDLEA paid a WADA advocacy visit to His Royal Majesty, King Couple Mackson Oromoni Mobene III, Pere Ama-Okosu of Ogbe-Ijoh Warri Kingdom, Delta state, among others,” he said.

Mr Babafemi quoted the NDLEA chairman, Buba Marwa, a retired brigadier general, as commending the officers and men of Lagos, Tincan, Edo, Niger, Delta, Ondo, Gombe, Imo and FCT Commands for their professionalism and intelligence-driven approach to the various successful operations.

Mr Marwa enjoined them and their colleagues across the country to continue the current balanced approach to the agency’s drug control efforts.

(NAN)

World.title: 2Baba’s kids, industry stars attend his 51st birthday album listening party, Natasha absent
World.content:
Music veteran Innocent “2Baba” Idibia previewed his forthcoming album, “Oldest Young Man”, on Saturday at a listening party held to mark his 51st birthday in Victoria Island, Lagos.

The event drew his children, mother, friends and prominent entertainment figures, including Kenny Ogungbe, Dayo “D1” Adeneye, Wande Coal, African China, Ayo Makun, Faze, Tony Tetuila, Jide Awobona and Spyro.

Natasha Osawaru, the Edo State lawmaker and 2Baba’s partner, was absent from the event. Her absence came amid continued reports about the state of their relationship. It was not immediately clear why she did not attend.

Also absent were the mothers of the singer’s children: actress Annie Macaulay, Sunmbo Adeoye and Pero Adeniyi.

Blackface, with whom the singer fell out due to long-running disputes over song ownership, royalties, and credit for major hits like “African Queen” and “Let Somebody Love You”, was also absent at the party.

2Baba announced his separation from Annie, with whom he has two daughters, in January 2025 after more than a decade of marriage. The couple married traditionally in Lagos in 2012 and held a widely publicised wedding ceremony in Dubai the following year.

Sunmbo, who has two sons with the singer, is now married to Pastor David Adeoye, founder and senior pastor of Royalty Christian Centre. Pero, who has three children with 2Baba, was also not seen at the gathering.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The singer’s children and his mother, Rose Idibia, joined him onstage to cut his birthday cake.

Guests were also treated to a nostalgic moment when 2Baba and Faze performed a freestyle that revisited their years as members of Plantashun Boiz. The performance drew loud applause from the audience.

The duo belonged to the group, along with Ahmedu “Blackface” Obiabo. Formed in the late 1990s, Plantashun Boiz became one of Nigeria’s influential music groups before its members pursued solo careers.

Album preview

Beyond the birthday festivities, the gathering gave guests a chance to hear songs from “Oldest Young Man” ahead of its official release.

The singer began his birthday activities on Friday with the release of “Mental”, a collaboration with singer Fave.

He also used the occasion to introduce 2Baba Jollof, a new food business representing another step into entrepreneurship for the music star.

Mallam Yankee, 2Baba’s manager, said the activities surrounding the birthday went beyond celebrating the singer’s new age, describing them as the beginning of a new phase in his career.

He said the new chapter would see 2Baba pursue more projects in the coming months while continuing to build on his decades-long music career.

Born on 18 September 1975, 2Baba rose to national prominence as a member of Plantashun Boiz before launching a successful solo career.

His 2004 debut solo album, Face 2 Face, featured “African Queen”, the hit song that helped establish him as one of the leading figures in contemporary African music.

Relationship speculation

The reported disagreement between 2Baba and Natasha came to public attention in August following an alleged confrontation at the launch of the ’90s Lounge in Abuja.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the incident fuelled speculation about tensions between the couple after a video from the venue circulated on social media.

The footage appeared to show Natasha and 2Baba during a confrontation, but it did not capture the events leading up to the encounter or establish the cause of the disagreement.

An eyewitness, however, claimed that Natasha arrived at the venue with a group of men and attempted to speak with the singer.

The witness alleged that she approached 2Baba’s vehicle after he arrived and asked to speak with him, leading to a commotion outside the lounge.

The development came shortly after 2Baba performed at Daddy Showkey’s “50 Years on Stage” celebration at Eko Hotels & Suites in Victoria Island, Lagos.

During that performance, the singer briefly referred to some of his recent experiences and said he was no longer interested in seeking trouble.

“I’ve decided not to look for trouble again. I’ve gone to look for trouble, and I’ve seen the trouble. Tell your neighbours never to look for trouble,” he said.

World.title: Nigeria vs Colombia: Five players who could decide crucial FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup Quarter-final clash
World.content:
Nigeria’s Falconets face one of their biggest tests yet at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland when they take on Colombia in a quarter-final clash with a place in the last four at stake.

The Falconets stormed into the quarter-finals with an emphatic 3-0 victory over England, producing arguably their most complete performance of the tournament.

Colombia, meanwhile, booked their place in the last eight after edging hosts Poland 1-0, setting up a fascinating encounter between two sides with different routes to the quarter-finals.

For Nigeria, the challenge now is to reproduce the intensity, discipline and attacking quality that overwhelmed England; with the stakes higher and the margin for error smaller, individual performances could ultimately decide who advances.

PREMIUM TIMES looks at five players to watch when the Falconets face Colombia

Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei

If Nigeria are to break down Colombia and secure a place in the semi-finals, Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei, the fresh winner of the MVP in the last game, could once again be at the heart of their attacking threat.

The Benfica Ladies striker produced one of her best performances of the tournament in 3 appearances against England, scoring Nigeria’s second goal of the game and her second of the tournament, just two minutes after the restart with a superb left-footed volley.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Her finish was not only technically impressive but also arrived at a crucial moment. England needed a response after Nigeria’s first-half advantage, but Akekoromowei’s early second-half strike effectively killed off any hopes of an immediate comeback.

Akekoromowei has also shown a willingness to test opposing goalkeepers. She entered the knockout stage among the tournament’s leading players for goal attempts, with 18 attempts and four on target, and that attacking instinct could be decisive against Colombia.

The South Americans have shown considerable defensive patience throughout the tournament, which means Nigeria may not have many clear opportunities.

When those opportunities arrive, Akekoromowei will be expected to make them count. Her movement, physical presence and ability to strike with either power or technique could provide Nigeria with the cutting edge required to unlock Colombia.

Ramotalahi Kareem

Ramotalahi Kareem might not have found the net since her hat-trick against Caledonia in the last game of the group stage. Still, she is another Nigerian player who could have a major influence on the quarter-final.

The Falconets will need players capable of stretching Colombia’s defensive structure, creating space, and keeping the South Americans occupied throughout the contest, and this was exactly what she brought to the pitch throughout her time on the pitch.

Against a Colombian team that has demonstrated a willingness to defend patiently and wait for counterattacks, Kareem’s movement could be particularly important, as Nigeria cannot afford to become predictable.

They will need to move the ball quickly, attack spaces, and create situations that force Colombia’s defenders to make difficult decisions.

With the Falconets now only one victory away from the semi-finals, her ability to make the most of the opportunities that come her way could become a major storyline.

Christiana Uzoma

At the other end of the pitch, Christiana Uzoma will have a major responsibility.

The Falconets’ captain was outstanding against England, producing several important saves before making one of the defining interventions of the match.

With Nigeria leading, Uzoma denied Princess Ademiluyi in a one-on-one situation before producing an even bigger moment by saving Rachel Maltby’s penalty.

She got down to the spot-kick and pushed the ball onto the crossbar, preserving Nigeria’s advantage and preventing England from finding a route back into the contest.

That kind of composure could be invaluable against Colombia, as fine margins often decide Quarter-final matches, and Colombia have already demonstrated their ability to remain patient until opportunities emerge.

Uzoma will therefore need to be alert throughout the game, as her command of the penalty area, reactions, and ability to handle pressure will be tested against a Colombian attack determined to punish any defensive lapse.

After her performance against England, Nigeria know they have a goalkeeper capable of keeping them in the game when the pressure rises.

Juana Ortegon

Colombia’s captain, Juana Ortegon, brings experience and leadership to a team that is once again chasing a deep run at the U-20 Women’s World Cup.

Ortegon was part of Colombia’s 2024 campaign and has returned to the tournament two years later with even greater responsibility. She is now the captain and will be expected to provide composure when Nigeria attempt to impose their physical and energetic style on the game.

Colombia reached the quarter-finals on home soil in 2024 before losing to the Netherlands on penalties.

That experience of knockout football could prove valuable against Nigeria, particularly if the contest remains tight deep into the second half.

Ortegon has also been part of the pathway towards Colombia’s senior national team, making the quarter-final another opportunity to demonstrate why she is regarded as one of the country’s emerging talents.

Her leadership could be particularly important if Colombia are forced to defend for extended periods, as Nigeria’s intensity will test the Colombian midfield, and Ortegon’s ability to help her team retain its shape and composure could have a major bearing on the contest.

Fernanda Viafara

Fernanda Viafara completes the five-player watchlist and represents another important piece of Colombia’s attacking and creative threat.

Viafara is part of a talented Colombian generation that has emerged through the country’s youth system and is now being closely monitored as a potential contributor to the senior national team.

Earlier, Colombia’s coach Carlos Paniagua identified Viafara alongside captain Juana Ortegon and Maithe Lopez as one of the young players capable of pushing towards the senior setup and potentially competing for places at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

That makes the quarter-final against Nigeria another significant stage for Viafara. Colombia will need players capable of finding solutions against a Nigerian team that will bring considerable physicality and intensity to the contest.

Viafara’s ability to operate in attacking areas and contribute to Colombia’s build-up could become important if the South Americans are forced to spend long periods defending.

Nigeria will be expected to press and attack with pace, but that can also create spaces for Colombia to exploit when possession changes hands, and Viafara could therefore become important in those transition moments. The Colombian side has already demonstrated that they are capable of remaining patient and waiting for opportunities to emerge.

If Nigeria commit numbers forward, Viafara will be among the players Colombia could rely on to turn those moments into attacking opportunities.

Her ability to maintain composure and make the right decision in the final third could be particularly valuable in a quarter-final where chances may be limited.

Battle of contrasting strengths

The quarter-final brings together two teams who have already shown different sides of their character in Poland.

Nigeria produced a statement performance against England, winning 3-0 through goals from Akekoromowei, Tosin Rafiu and Mary Mamudu. At the same time, Uzoma’s penalty save helped ensure the Falconets maintained control when England threatened to respond.

Colombia, meanwhile, had to grind out their victory against hosts Poland, eventually advancing through a late own goal. That contrast could make the quarter-final particularly intriguing.

Nigeria have the attacking confidence that comes from scoring three times against England, but Colombia have shown that they can remain patient and competitive in a tight knockout contest.

The South Americans will also have to contend with Nigeria’s physicality, pace and attacking movement; for the Falconets, the challenge will be to avoid frustration if Colombia sit deep and deny them space. That is where players such as Akekoromowei and Kareem could become decisive.

If Nigeria can find their attacking rhythm while maintaining the defensive discipline that served them so well against England, they will give themselves a strong platform to progress.

But Colombia will have their own weapons, with Ortegon providing leadership. Viafara poses an attacking threat capable of exploiting any gaps, and at this stage of the competition, there is little room for error.

One piece of individual brilliance, one defensive error or one crucial save could decide the tie.

For the Falconets, victory would take them into the semi-finals for the first time since 2014 and move them another step closer to finally ending their long wait for the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup title.

World.title: Osimhen ruled out of Super Eagles’ AFCON qualifiers
World.content:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen will miss Nigeria’s opening two 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau after failing to recover from a muscle strain.

The Nigeria national team confirmed his withdrawal on Saturday after the Galatasaray forward was absent from his club’s 4-0 defeat to Trabzonspor in the Turkish Süper Lig.

According to the Super Eagles media team, Osimhen’s recovery has taken longer than initially expected.

“Victor Osimhen’s recovery from a muscle strain has been slower than expected. He was included in Nigeria’s squad for the AFCON qualifiers because Galatasaray and Super Eagles technical crew were hopeful he would be fit for the Super Lig game versus Trabzonspor and ready for the international window. But his absence from tonight’s match confirms Galatasaray’s correspondence to Super Eagles manager Eric Chelle that the striker is still recovering and will not be ready for Nigeria’s matches.”

Osimhen was named in Éric Chelle’s 24-man squad for the qualifiers against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau when the list was announced on Thursday.

Nigeria will host Madagascar’s Barea at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday, 25 September, before travelling to Bissau to face Guinea-Bissau’s Wild Dogs on Tuesday, 29 September.

His withdrawal leaves Chelle without one of his main attacking options as Nigeria begin their qualification campaign.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Injury setback

Osimhen suffered the injury during Galatasaray’s 3-2 victory over Istanbul Basaksehir on 4 September, scoring before leaving the match after 33 minutes.

Galatasaray subsequently announced that medical examinations revealed a moderate-to-advanced strain, with bleeding, in his right adductor muscle group, and that treatment had begun.

The injury has already kept him out of Galatasaray’s Champions League meeting with Sporting CP and a Süper Lig fixture against Kocaelispor.

His absence from Saturday’s match against Trabzonspor effectively ended hopes that he would recover in time to join Nigeria for the September international window.

READ ALSO: Iheanacho equals Bursaspor record as Super Eagles striker continues stunning run in Turkey

Osimhen’s inclusion in Chelle’s initial squad had reflected the expectation that he could recover in time. The NFF’s announcement listed him alongside captain Wilfred Ndidi, Alex Iwobi, Ademola Lookman, and Moses Simon as one of the established players retained for the qualifiers.

Chelle has attacking options

With Osimhen unavailable, Chelle still has several attacking options in the squad, including Lookman, Moses Simon, Akor Adams, Samuel Chukwueze, Tolu Arokodare, George Ilenikhena and Moses Usor.

Nigeria are grouped with Madagascar, Guinea-Bissau and Tanzania in the 2027 AFCON qualifying series. Tanzania, as one of the tournament co-hosts, already have an automatic place at the finals, leaving the qualifying race in the group to determine the other participant.

World.title: 2027: SERAP sues INEC over alleged failure to disclose political donation limits, party finances
World.content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has filed a lawsuit against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “over its failure to disclose the limits on political contributions under section 91 of the Electoral Act 2026, including whether the Commission has exercised its statutory power to set such limits and, if so, why the applicable limits have not been publicly disclosed and communicated to political parties, candidates, donors and Nigerians.”

The lawsuit followed INEC’s alleged failure to disclose whether it has prescribed limits on political contributions under section 91 of the Electoral Act 2026. Such limits are important safeguards for transparency, accountability and fair electoral competition. Their non-disclosure leaves Nigerians unclear about the rules governing political donations and raises questions about compliance with the law.

In the suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/2114/2026 filed last week at the Federal High Court in Abuja, SERAP is seeking: “an order of mandamus to direct and compel INEC to urgently disclose whether it has prescribed limits on political contributions, the specific limits prescribed, and the measures taken to publish and communicate them to political parties, candidates, donors and the public.”

SERAP is also seeking: “an order of mandamus to direct and compel INEC to disclose the systems and procedures in place to monitor, investigate and enforce compliance with prescribed limits on political contributions and campaign expenditure, particularly in preparation for the 2027 general elections.”

In the suit, SERAP is arguing that: “greater transparency in political financing is essential to ensuring that the 2027 elections are conducted on a level playing field and that citizens are able to make free and informed political choices.”

SERAP is also arguing that: “INEC’s constitutional responsibility is not simply to receive financial statements from political parties. The Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended) requires the Commission to examine political-party finances, conduct necessary investigations and report to the National Assembly.”

According to SERAP, “publishing these reports would enable Nigerians to know whether these constitutional and statutory responsibilities have been effectively discharged.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The lawsuit filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Oluwakemi Agunbiade, Kehinde Oyewumi, Andrew Nwankwo and Valentina Adegoke, reads in part: “Voters, journalists and civil-society organisations cannot effectively scrutinise political financing if the applicable limits are not easily accessible or if there is no publicly known mechanism for monitoring compliance.”

“The increasing monetisation of Nigeria’s elections, alongside the potential misuse of state institutions, poses serious threats to democratic integrity and electoral competition.”

“INEC should be compelled to disclose and publish the political-contribution limits prescribed under section 91 of the Electoral Act, 2026, as well as political parties’ latest financial statements, audited accounts, sources of funds, assets, liabilities and election-expenditure returns for 2023–2025.”

“INEC should also be compelled to disclose its examination and audit reports under sections 225 and 226, including reports submitted to the National Assembly, and details of enforcement action taken for political-finance violations.”

“The Court should further compel INEC to disclose its political-finance monitoring and enforcement arrangements for the 2027 general elections, including the parties that submitted post-2023 contribution reports, the dates of submission, and action taken against parties that failed to comply with statutory reporting requirements.”

“The reliefs sought would enable citizens to identify excessive, undisclosed or potentially illicit political financing before it can distort electoral competition, rather than only after votes have been cast.”

“Effective political-finance regulation is an important safeguard for constitutional democracy, equality of political participation, freedom of expression and association, electoral integrity and citizens’ meaningful participation in public affairs.”

“Nigeria has a persistent problem of political parties failing to disclose campaign contributions. Such non-compliance has been described as systemic, while the absence of clear and effective sanctions for default has weakened INEC’s ability to enforce compliance.”

“Nigeria has long faced serious challenges in regulating political finance, including concerns about excessive campaign spending, opaque sources of political funding, weak disclosure and reporting, and limited enforcement of statutory spending and contribution rules.”

“Previous assessments of Nigeria’s elections have identified significant gaps between the legal framework and its practical implementation, including concerns that spending limits can be circumvented, political-party expenditure is insufficiently regulated or transparently disclosed, and violations are rarely identified and effectively sanctioned.”

“These concerns are particularly significant given the scale of campaign expenditure and changes in the statutory spending and contribution thresholds under Nigeria’s constitutional and evolving electoral framework.”

“It remains unclear whether INEC has prescribed, clearly published and effectively monitored the applicable contribution limits, and whether political parties and candidates can be held accountable for contributions and expenditure that exceed applicable limits or are deliberately concealed.”

“Transparency about the financial affairs of political parties is particularly important because political parties are central to the exercise of citizens’ constitutional rights to participate in public affairs and to form and belong to political associations.”

“Citizens cannot meaningfully exercise their political rights if undisclosed or excessive financial resources are allowed to distort the political process.”

“Political parties, candidates and their supporters are already mobilising resources, soliciting contributions, organising political activities, purchasing media and digital advertising, holding rallies and other events, and incurring campaign-related expenditure.”

“INEC should disclose how it intends to monitor political financing during the campaign period, including expenditure and contributions involving cash and in-kind contributions; digital and social-media advertising; political consultants and campaign consultants; and third-party campaign expenditure.”

“The existence of statutory limits on political contributions and election expenditure is intended not merely to facilitate retrospective accounting after an election but to prevent excessive financial influence while political competition is taking place.”

“Section 91(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 provides that: ‘The Commission shall have power to place limitation on the amount of money or other assets which an individual can contribute to a political party or candidate and to demand such information on the amount donated and source of the funds.’”

“Section 91(2) provides sanctions where an individual, candidate or political party exceeds the applicable limit prescribed by INEC. The statutory power given to INEC creates an important safeguard against excessive financial influence over political parties and candidates.”

“Where INEC has exercised its power under section 91, Nigerians are entitled to know the applicable contribution limits and how the Commission intends to ensure compliance with them.”

“INEC should clarify whether it has prescribed contribution limits and, if so, immediately publish them in a prominent and easily accessible location, including on its website.”

“INEC should explain the methodology and criteria used in determining the limits and whether the Commission has considered the need to prevent excessive financial influence, ensure fair electoral competition, address risks of corruption and illicit political financing, and protect the integrity of the electoral process.”

“Section 226(1) of the Nigerian Constitution imposes an annual obligation on INEC to prepare and submit to the National Assembly a report on the accounts and balance sheets of political parties.”

“Section 226(2) requires INEC to conduct investigations necessary to enable it to form an opinion on whether proper books of account and proper records have been maintained by political parties.”

“Section 226(3) gives INEC and its duly authorised agents access to the books, accounts and vouchers of political parties and enables them to require information and explanations necessary for the discharge of these constitutional responsibilities.”

“INEC has commenced the formal preparations for the 2027 General Elections, marking an important stage in the electoral process.”

“Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) guarantees citizens the right to participate in public affairs and to vote and be elected at genuine periodic elections. Article 9 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights protects the right to receive information, while Article 13 guarantees the right to participate freely in the government of one’s country.”

No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

World.title: Nigerian hospitals collaborate to perform tele-robotic surgery
World.content:
The Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV), in collaboration with RoboMed Global and Nisa Premier Hospital, has performed what it described as Nigeria’s first tele-robotic surgery.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the surgery was performed in real time on Saturday from a Toumai console at RHV on a patient at Nisa Premier Hospital, Abuja.

The procedure was a telesurgery-assisted, robot-assisted right radical nephrectomy performed to remove a kidney affected by a cancerous tumour.

Tele-robotic surgery, also known as remote surgery, is a technique that enables a surgeon to perform an operation on a patient from a completely different physical location.

Speaking after the surgery at RHV, Obi Ekwenna-Davis, professor of Urology and Transplantation, who led the surgery, explained the medical condition of the patient.

He said the procedure demonstrated that telesurgery could be safely performed on patients in different parts of Nigeria and the world.

Mr Ekwenna-Davis, co-founder of RoboMed Global, said the development was a significant achievement for RHV and its partners.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Distance should never decide who receives safe surgery; this is what safe and trusted surgery looks like,” he said.

The US-based surgeon said the patient was in good condition and expected to be discharged within 24 hours.

He said the procedure lasted about three hours, with brief stoppages to ensure that the equipment and systems functioned properly.

Mr Ekwenna-Davis said the collaboration was significant as it marked the first time two hospitals in different parts of Nigeria successfully collaborated to provide surgical care to a patient.

He said the sustainability of the initiative would depend on continuous training, adding that a robotic academy would soon be established to train surgeons and other medical professionals.

According to him, the academy aims to train at least 150 surgeons within the next two years.

Mr Ekwenna-Davis said the programme had the support of the Minister of Health and other government institutions, while calling for additional support from private and non-governmental organisations.

Earlier, Adedamola Dada, chief executive officer of RHV, said the development marked the first telesurgery in West Africa.

Mr Dada said RHV was established to promote innovation and provide world-class healthcare services at affordable costs.

“What has happened today is a demonstration that Nigerians can access modern healthcare without travelling abroad,” he said.

He said the initiative was not primarily profit-driven but aimed at demonstrating what modern healthcare could offer Nigerians, in line with the vision of the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God.

Mr Dada said the achievement had positioned the hospital as a gateway through which specialist skills could be transferred to patients across Nigeria.

He said the introduction of robotic surgery and telesurgery at RHV was aimed at reducing medical tourism and improving access to complex surgical procedures within the country.

The CEO said measures had been put in place to address possible connectivity challenges through the use of reliable networks.

He explained that weather conditions could sometimes affect connectivity, while the quality of equipment and availability of skilled personnel were also critical to the success of telesurgery.

Dada said the hospital was establishing a robotic academy in collaboration with RoboMed Global to train doctors, surgeons, nurses, biomedical engineers and product specialists.

He urged the government to support and sponsor medical professionals interested in acquiring robotic surgery skills.

“My message to government is to support and sponsor Nigerians, the surgeons, the nurses, the biomedical engineers who would want to come and do this training here.

“They can award scholarships to them so that within two to three years, Nigeria will have a lot of professionals who are capable of performing robotic surgery,” he said.

Ibrahim Wada, chief executive officer and founder of Nisa Premier Hospital, said the facility had been a centre for robotic surgery in West Africa since November 2025.

“Today, our patient received specialist surgical expertise from across the country without leaving Abuja. This is what becomes possible when Nigerian institutions decide to build together,” Wada said.

Also, Kunle Onakoya, chairman of the Board of RHV, described the development as historic and urged participants to recognise their roles in creating a milestone for Nigeria.

NAN reports that RHV is a faith-based 300-bed multispecialty hospital established by the Redeemed Christian Church of God.

NAN also reports that journalists watched the procedure live on television at RHV.

(NAN)

World.title: APC wins Dawakin Kudu constituency by-election in Kano
World.content:

World.title: RHV, Nisa Premier Hospitals perform first tele-robotic surgery in West Africa
World.content:
By Chioma obinna

A new chapter opened in Nigeria’s healthcare system at the weekend as surgeons at Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Hospital, Lagos, in collaboration with Nisa Premier Hospital, Abuja, successfully performed what they described as the first tele-robotic surgery in West Africa.

The landmark procedure saw a surgeon in Lagos remotely operate on a patient undergoing surgery at Nisa Premier Hospital in Abuja, demonstrating for the first time the possibility of delivering complex surgical care across hundreds of kilometres without the operating surgeon being physically present at the patient’s location.

The procedure, witnessed by selected journalists at RHV in Lagos, involved a patient with a kidney tumour in Abuja. Using robotic surgical technology and a high-speed internet connection, the surgical team in Lagos controlled the robotic system at the Abuja hospital to perform the operation.

Robotic Surgeon from RoboMed Global Inc., a US-based company and a Professor of Urology and Transplantation, Obi Davies-Ekwenna, described the development as a significant demonstration of what technology could bring to healthcare delivery in Nigeria.

“The second procedure we did was a tele-surgery procedure where we were able to operate on a patient in Abuja, 500 kilometres away. We were able to operate on a patient with a kidney tumour, a cancer tumour. And so that was successful.”

The tele-robotic operation followed another robotic procedure performed on a 28-year-old woman who had lived with a congenital obstruction affecting the drainage of her kidney.

Speaking with journalists shortly after the surgeries, the Chief Executive Officer of RHV Hospital, Dr Adedamola Dada, said the patient’s condition had placed her kidney at risk of permanent damage.

According to him, the robotic procedure was used to remove the obstruction and reconstruct the affected area to restore the normal flow of urine.

“For those of us who were in the theatre, it was pretty obvious immediately that the obstruction was removed. The urine started flowing very freely,” Dada said.

He said the procedure itself lasted about one-and-a-half hours, excluding preparations for the robotic system, and resulted in minimal blood loss.

“For me, the most important thing is the quality of the work that has been done. The surgery is a lot more precise, the bleeding is almost no bleeding, and the patient can go home early.”

Dada said the significance of the development went beyond the two patients, arguing that remote robotic surgery could expand access to highly specialised medical care in Nigeria.

He said the technology could eventually allow specialists in other parts of Nigeria, or even abroad, to perform complex procedures on patients without requiring them to travel.

“What this simply means is that for very complicated cases where we don’t even have the manpower in-country, surgeons can stay in the US and operate on that patient here,” he said.

“This is a new day for our country.”

The RHV chief executive also said the technology could help reduce the pressure of medical tourism by allowing Nigerians to access advanced procedures locally.

He disclosed that RHV was also developing a robotic academy to train surgeons, operating theatre nurses, biomedical engineers and other specialists needed to sustain robotic surgery in Nigeria.

Also, Chairman of the Board of RHV Hospital, Dr Kunle Onokoya said robotic surgery represented a major evolution from conventional surgical procedures.

He recalled that during his training in the 1980s, some operations could require patients to remain in hospital for about 10 days, with bleeding and infection among the major concerns.

“Fast forward to today, the patient is going to go home today, worst case tomorrow. Bleeding is minimal,” Onokoya said.

He explained that although robots perform the physical movements, they remain under the control of highly trained surgeons.

“The robot is still being controlled by a human being, by a very, very experienced and senior surgeon. It is just that the skills of that surgeon are now being magnified many times over by the robot,” he said.

Davis- Ekwenna said the achievement was the result of collaboration between Nigerian surgeons, engineers, nurses and international partners.

He said the programme was designed not only to perform robotic procedures but also to develop local capacity.

“Our engineers were Nigerians, our surgeons were Nigerians, the nurses are Nigerian,” he said.

According to him, the team hopes to train at least 150 surgeons in robotic surgery within the next two years.

He added that robotic surgery offers patients less pain, fewer complications, reduced infections and faster recovery.

The development, he said, demonstrated that patients across Nigeria could potentially gain access to specialised surgical expertise regardless of their location.

“We just scratched the surface today to show that this can be done. Patients in Nigeria, regardless of where they live, can have access to the best surgical care in the world here in Nigeria, done by Nigerians,” he said.

World.title: Plateau attacks: Women, children flee Barkin Ladi as gunshots persist
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa

Tension has gripped Dorowa Bubuje community in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, as women and children are being evacuated from the area following renewed gunshots reportedly heard from the direction of Kantoma.

The development has forced residents to retreat from parts of the community, with groups of women and children moving to safer locations as security personnel continue efforts to contain the situation.

Lawrence Shong, a member of the community, told Vanguard that gunshots had continued in the Kantoma area, prompting residents to gather and move away from locations considered vulnerable to attack.

“As I speak to you, at about 12:15pm on Sunday, we are still hearing sounds of gunshots,” he said.

According to him, “Women and children are currently being evacuated because of the ongoing attack. We are still hearing gunshots, and this is forcing people to retreat.”

“Currently, our people are gathering and moving away from this place. The women and children are being taken to safer locations.”

He lauded the military for repelling attacks in some other communities in the local government..

Meanwhile, spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, who was at the community, told Vanguard that the situation remained tense, with residents moving away from areas considered vulnerable.”

Tengwong said the continued gunshots had heightened anxiety among residents and forced families to seek safer locations.”

He said, “Currently, women and children are being evacuated from this place because of the ongoing attack. “

“We are still hearing gunshots from the direction of Kantoma, and that is forcing people to retreat.”

“That is why you are seeing people gathering and moving away. The women and children are the first people being moved to safer locations.”

“Military personnel have been drafted to the community, and what we need now is sustained security deployment to protect the people and prevent further attacks.”

Tengwong commended the military and other security operatives for their response, saying their intervention helped prevent further escalation.

He appealed for sustained security presence in the affected communities, saying this would enable residents to return to their homes without fear.

Efforts to reach security operatives for further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

Our correspondent reports that alt least nine persons have been killed in separate attacks in Barkin Ladi, Riyom and neighbouring communities in Plateau State between Saturday night and Sunday morning, with tensions mounting in the affected areas.

Five of the victims were passengers travelling to Gana-Ropp in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area when they were attacked on Saturday night, while two others, including a pastor, were reportedly killed while on their way to church at Dorowa Babuje on Sunday morning.

World.title: Ex-England winger Townsend run over by pitch roller in Thailand
World.content:
Former England international Andros Townsend was partially run over by a pitch roller in Thai football, but avoided serious injury in the bizarre incident.

The 35-year-old former Spurs winger was warming up for PT Prachuap’s game at Pattani on Saturday when the driver lost control of the vehicle.

Townsend went down under the heavy roller, with the driver only stopping once the player’s legs were trapped.

In footage which has since been widely shared online, Townsend attempts to push the roller off as the driver leaps out to help.

Townsend, who also played for Crystal Palace and Everton during an itinerant career, later made light of being run over.

“It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad after all,” he wrote on social media.

Townsend won 13 caps for England.

World.title: 2027: APC group warns Obi, NDC over result transmission
World.content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — A pro-All Progressives Congress (APC) group, Renewed Hope for Greater Nigeria (RHGN), has urged the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to clarify plans for independently transmitting polling-unit election results during the 2027 general elections.

The group warned against what it described as an attempt to establish a parallel electoral results system, saying such an arrangement could create confusion over the authority of official election results.

Deputy National Leader, South-East, of RHGN, Mazi Franklin Ngoforo, raised the concern while briefing journalists in Umuahia, Abia State.

His reaction followed an interview Obi granted Arise News on September 10, 2026, during which the NDC presidential candidate said his team would deploy a system to independently receive results from polling units at its situation room alongside transmission to the designated Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) platform.

Obi said the proposed arrangement was intended to enable his team to independently monitor results and ensure that figures announced were consistent with those recorded at polling units.

He also rejected the suggestion that the plan amounted to establishing a parallel INEC, saying it was intended to provide an independent means of monitoring the electoral process.

However, Ngoforo said the proposal required clarification, particularly on who would operate the additional system, its legal basis and the role it would play in the electoral process.

He also referred to an earlier statement attributed to Professor Pat Utomi concerning an independent election-results transmission arrangement ahead of the 2027 elections, saying the two developments warranted public scrutiny.

Ngoforo challenged the NDC to explain whether the proposed system was intended solely as a transparency and monitoring mechanism or as an alternative channel for establishing election results.

He argued that the conduct and management of elections remained within the constitutional mandate of INEC.

“The Electoral Act 2026 goes further by specifically prescribing how election results are to be transmitted and managed,” he said.

Under Section 60(3) of the Electoral Act 2026, presiding officers are required to electronically transmit polling-unit results to the IReV portal after the prescribed Form EC8A has been completed and signed. The law also provides for a fallback where electronic transmission fails, with the signed Form EC8A remaining the primary source for collation and declaration.

Ngoforo said the statutory framework should be respected by all political parties and candidates, while acknowledging the right of stakeholders to demand transparent elections and effective monitoring.

“Every Nigerian wants credible elections. Every Nigerian wants his vote to count. But the answer cannot be to create rival electoral authorities,” he said.

He called on the Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Office of the National Security Adviser and other relevant agencies to seek clarification from the NDC and Obi on the proposed independent transmission arrangement.

According to him, the agencies should determine the nature and purpose of any system being developed and ensure that political parties operate within the existing constitutional and statutory framework.

Ngoforo also warned against any action that could contribute to confusion or violence during the 2027 electoral process.

“We must not wait until Nigeria is on fire before we begin asking questions,” he said.

The RHGN official urged political parties and candidates to channel their efforts towards strengthening confidence in the electoral process rather than creating competing systems that could, in his view, generate uncertainty over the status of election results.

World.title: U-20 Women’s World Cup: 1 semi-final fixture confirmed as Nigeria face Colombia
World.content:
Italy and Spain have secured their places in the semi-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, as Nigeria look to take on Colombia in the quarter-finals.

Italy booked their spot in the last four with a 3-1 victory over South Korea in Saturday’s quarter-final.
