World.title: Estonian experts say social media should be improved for children instead of banned
World.content:
The European Union is discussing a safe‑internet regulation that includes several restrictions planned for minors' use of social media. While EU plans propose setting a minimum age of 13, Estonian social scientists argue that blunt bans will not solve all problems and may even create new ones.

Tallinn University media professor Indrek Ibrus is critical of the EU initiative, saying the planned restrictions conflict with children's fundamental rights.

"In my opinion, it's generally a pretty bad idea," Ibrus said, explaining that it ignores the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. "Children must have opportunities for self‑expression and free access to information to support their development and identity. Any age‑based restriction on access to information essentially disregards children's rights," Ibrus said.

According to Ibrus, the European Commission is effectively giving up by proposing restrictions.

Indrek Ibrus. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

"Instead of working on these environments, these platforms, these spaces in a way that would make them safe and suitable for children, the European Commission throws up its hands and gives up. They don't have the strength to deal with regulation, even though the regulatory framework — the Digital Services Act — already exists and simply needs to be enforced. In a sense, children are being sacrificed because of the Commission's own inability," he said.

University of Tartu media studies professor Andra Siibak agreed that relying solely on bans and restrictions is not the best solution, highlighting the need to change platform business models. Siibak said it is positive that the EU demands concrete measures from service providers to make platforms more protective of children's rights, well‑being and privacy.

Like Ibrus, Siibak pointed out that all these recommended changes are already written into earlier EU regulations — whether the Digital Services Act or the AI Act. "The European Union itself must start thinking carefully about how to demand these changes from platforms and monitor that they actually implement them," Siibak said.

Andra Siibak Autor/allikas: ERR/Lauri Varik

Tallinn University participation‑culture professor Katrin Tiidenberg warned against overly rigid bans, citing Australia's experience.

"Based on what we know from Australia and how their ban doesn't actually work, children under 16 are still online, which mainly means we don't know what they're doing on social media or where they're logged in," Tiidenberg said.

One of the biggest questions surrounding the EU Kids Act is how to verify users' ages without massively violating people's privacy.

Ibrus sees major risks in age verification. "It may be a direct privacy intrusion, and it may also be harmful in the sense that platforms could use identification for more precise profiling of users, which can be dangerous in several ways," he explained.

Ibrus added that although the EU is developing a digital wallet solution that could provide secure infrastructure in the future, any restrictions must be approached with extreme caution.

Siibak also noted that finding a reliable and transparent age‑verification method is currently difficult. Attempts with facial‑recognition software have not worked, and young people easily bypass restrictions using, for example, their parents' documents.

"We know from Australia's experience how skillfully young people bypass such age‑assessment apps and solutions. To access a platform, they show their parents' documents or take a photo with a famous footballer's poster in the background instead of showing their own face. Young people certainly have many ways to get around such systems. Finding a method acceptable to all member states will be a very difficult discussion," Siibak said.

Katrin Tiidenberg Autor/allikas: Priit Mürk/ERR

Tiidenberg also stressed that mechanical age‑verification methods bring risks. "It's a very important issue, because if it means a child must log in with an ID card, then it means everyone must log in with an ID card. We want to avoid mass surveillance and monitoring of which sites we visit and who does what. In my view, maintaining freedom is important," Tiidenberg said.

"That doesn't mean age verification cannot be done in a reasonably safe way, but the method must be developed very carefully and not by quickly trusting the first private company that says: 'Look, I built you a solution,'" Tiidenberg said.

Experts say protecting children and young people on social media should focus on improving the platforms themselves.

Tiidenberg highlighted the need to pressure platforms to create well‑being‑oriented and responsible design. This means placing strong emphasis on curbing addictive algorithms — for example, giving users the option to choose between a chronological feed and recommendation algorithms. She also supports separate child‑ and youth‑friendly accounts (for example, ages 13–15) where harmful content is automatically limited.

Ibrus reminded that in addition to tightening rules, it is important to support young people's digital skills and critical thinking instead of creating artificial barriers that do not actually protect them online.

"Instead of bluntly banning communication environments because they may involve certain risks, those risks must be addressed. Platforms must be adapted, regulated, existing regulations enforced, and at the same time media literacy must be developed for different age and social groups," Ibrus said.

Tiidenberg added that digital skills are important, but a person can be both competent and helpless at the same time — including children.

"Critical awareness is very important, but obviously children have different self‑regulation abilities at different ages. Even many adults do not have very good self‑regulation. You may know something is harmful to you, but you still may not be able to avoid certain social media content," she said.

"Skills are important — they are part of the toolkit — but they are not enough if we allow user interfaces to be designed manipulatively, because they still measure the user's slowing finger while scrolling. If we do not regulate how quickly systems must respond when I say that I or my child does not want to see certain content, then digital skills alone are of little use," Tiidenberg added.

On Thursday, the European Commission adopted the safe‑internet regulation (EU Kids Act), which increases children's online safety in the EU. The package includes proposals to ban social media use for children under 13 and to require companies providing online services to create safe accounts for children.

Under the proposal — which EU member states and the European Parliament will negotiate — accounts for children aged 13–15 would be under parental control.

Social media and video services, online games and AI‑based companions and chatbots intended for users under 18 would be subject to a list of permitted and prohibited activities.

World.title: Reintroduced dormice face a fox that moved to predator‑free island
World.content:
The garden dormice released on Suur‑Pakri Island this summer to rewild the species have encountered an unexpected co‑inhabitant who may consider the newcomers gourmet food.

The garden dormouse (Eliomys quercinus), a native Estonian species, went extinct in Estonia due to human activity. The exact cause is unknown. The last wild garden dormouse was seen in 1986. Around the same time, the species disappeared from neighboring countries as well. This summer, the first small colony was released on Suur‑Pakri Island.

"When we last left the island a couple of weeks ago, more than half of the 20 animals released were definitely alive. For a small zoo animal, that's a surprisingly good result. We're optimistic that maybe they'll even survive until spring," said ecologist Marko Mägi.

"Since it's a small animal with a very short lifespan and could end up in a predator's jaws during winter — even though it sleeps through winter — we don't know whether any of them will still see daylight in spring," Mägi noted.

Suur‑Pakri was chosen for reintroduction because it lacked predators.

"Last autumn we carried out control surveys and studied small mammals to determine whether the island was safe for garden dormice. At that time we could say there were no predators that would threaten them. We had a very harsh winter that covered the sea with ice, and a fox easily crossed over to the island," Mägi explained.

"This summer we discovered that a fox is indeed on the island. We saw it on trail cameras, and it was also spotted running through the forest. Now we're curious to see what happens by spring: will the fox win, or the garden dormice?"

"Although the garden dormouse is active at night and gladly climbs trees, where a fox cannot reach, their paths may still cross. But fortunately for the dormice, the island has plenty of other small rodents that interest the fox more. For the fox, the garden dormouse would be a true gourmet meal," Mägi said.

World.title: NATO has 4,000-page plans for escalation on eastern flank
World.content:
Responding to a journalist's question about a possible low-intensity provocation and the deployment of additional personnel and capabilities to NATO's eastern flank, Dragone said this was one of NATO's many plans.

"We have plans for the eastern flank — three plans, to be precise — to be ready for any kind of escalation," he said, noting that the plans cover actions, movements and countermeasures.

He said the decision-making process has been standardized to ensure it works as quickly as possible, and that this work has already begun. NATO has plans covering everything from a minor crisis or intervention on alliance territory to the invocation of Article 5 and beyond.

"The plans are ready, the structure is ready, and the troops, systems and weapons are on standby," Dragone said. "In the event of an attack, we know what to do," he added, saying that in the event of an attack, the risks of losses would far outweigh any potential gains.

Responding to a journalist's question about a possible Russian attack on border crossings between Poland and Ukraine, Dragone said NATO is already quite accustomed to hybrid attacks and, in his assessment, is dealing with them successfully. He noted that NATO is a defensive alliance and that the possibility of escalation is part of its thinking and approach. At the same time, Dragone said a direct attack on the Polish-Ukrainian border area has not been discussed as a realistic scenario.

"We have to demonstrate strength and send the message that no part of our territory, not a single centimeter of it, can come under attack," he said. Dragone explained that hybrid operations do not automatically trigger Article 5 of the NATO treaty because they generally remain below that threshold. "A direct attack is not on our agenda in the sense that we are planning for it, but in the event of a direct attack, the immediate invocation of Article 5 would be requested," he said.

Speaking about ammunition stocks in the event of a possible prolonged conflict with Russia, Dragone acknowledged that NATO is fully aware of the issue, particularly given the war in Ukraine and the enormous amount of ammunition both sides use every day. He said this is precisely why NATO is investing in and encouraging the defense industry to change — moving away from the peacetime mentality that prevailed just four years ago and increasing production capacity so that the industry is prepared for a prolonged war and can meet the necessary demand.

According to Dragone, the financial resources are available, as allies have decided to invest significantly more in defense. "The funding will be provided, and we need to accelerate their delivery capacity," he said. He said the defense industry is working on this and moving in the right direction, but efforts must be intensified further because the daily expenditure of weapons and ammunition is very high.

At the same time, other activities are taking place on the eastern flank involving both the use of drones and defenses against them. These activities are part of measures aimed at strengthening security on the eastern flank in all respects, from air defense and drone use to counter-drone capabilities.

Responding to a question about physical attacks on European defense industry factories and warehouses, Dragone said such incidents could be regarded as criminal offenses, but they could also be elements of hybrid warfare. He said intelligence services are dealing with the issue, but NATO does not know how many incidents have been prevented or thwarted before they occurred, partly because they are not reported. According to him, there have been many cases in which threats have been prevented or stopped in time, but the exact number of such cases is unknown.

"In defense, the results are not immediately visible or tangible. That is what security is," Dragone said, urging people to trust the work of the security services.

Dragone's remarks came at a meeting of NATO chiefs of defense in Copenhagen, Delfi reported, and followed warnings from several European leaders that Russia could stage a drone or missile attack against a NATO country supporting Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Thursday that Moscow could send drones or missiles into the territory of an eastern flank country as part of a staged provocation, an assessment echoed by French President Emmanuel Macron and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten. NATO's official threat assessment has not changed, and a NATO representative told Politico there is currently no imminent threat of attack.

World.title: Six French ISIS suspects face trial in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi court launched on Sunday the trial of six French nationals suspected of membership in the terrorist group ISIS.

A member of the Supreme Judicial Council warned that the suspects might face the death sentence if convicted of crimes against Iraq and its people.

According to two court legal sources, the defendants were among 47 French ISIS inmates relocated from prisons in northeast Syria in 2025 as part of an operation authorized by US forces and Iraqi officials.

According to Reuters, officials from the French embassy in Iraq were present at the Baghdad criminal court.

The six inmates being tried under Iraq’s counter-terrorism law arrived in the court in a prison van accompanied by a convoy of Humvees carrying Iraqi Special Forces officers.

The suspects were wearing yellow prison jumpsuits.

The judge in charge postponed the hearing until October 5 to allow defense lawyers to study the case files.

Abbas al-Maliki, a court-appointed solicitor for one of the prisoners, told Reuters that his client was facing allegations of ISIS membership.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

Earlier this month, the Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq announced that it officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

World.title: Iraq opens restricted air zones for civilian aviation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has lifted its decade-long military restrictions on western airspace, returning full control to civilian authorities.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport announced on Friday that it has fully eliminated the restricted zones, thereby restoring complete sovereignty over the country’s airspace.

Iraq’s General Company for Air Navigation Services (GCANS) now controls all previously restricted military zones, which range from the northern province of Nineveh to the southern desert in Anbar province.

Between 2016 and 2017, the airspace was restricted to civilian planes. The Iraqi Air Force and the US-led international coalition used it only for combat missions against ISIS.

The decision would enable foreign airlines to use shorter and more efficient international flight corridors. The decision is expected to reduce operational rates for global airlines and simultaneously boost transit charge revenue for the Iraqi government.

The Transport Ministry in Iraq announced that the removal of these restrictions is part of the withdrawal process, as Iraq and the United States work together to coordinate the departure of the US-led international coalition’s remaining forces.

Technical and legal alignment for completely integrating the newly available routes into civilian flight is projected to be completed by October 1, 2026.

World.title: US dollar eases below 160,000 IQD across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar experienced a slight retreat across parallel currency exchanges in Iraq on Sunday, September 20, 2026, dipping marginally below the 160,000-dinar mark recorded over the weekend while continuing to trade at a substantial premium above the official state benchmark.

According to market data, parallel bureaus across major trading hubs posted quotes well above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 131,000 dinars per $100.

In the capital city of Baghdad, exchange bureaus quoted selling rates at 159,750 dinars per $100, with buying rates settling at 159,000 dinars.

Trading across northern financial desks in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, reflected a slightly softer posture, posting selling prices of 158,700 dinars per $100 against buying levels of 158,250 dinars. In the southern economic hub of Basra, rates closely aligned with northern counters, recording 159,000 dinars for sale and 158,500 dinars for purchase.

While the day’s trades reflect a fractional cooling of roughly 250 to 950 dinars compared to Saturday’s peak surges, currency desks continue to price in significant liquidity risk.

The persistent spread between the parallel exchanges and the statutory peg highlights ongoing domestic cash-flow constraints and defensive trading behavior among market participants ahead of the critical September 30 deadline.

World.title: Washington Institute urges sanctions on Maliki, and Ameri over disarmament delays
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A policy analysis published by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy has recommended that the United States prepare targeted individual sanctions against former Iraqi Prime Minister Nouri Al-Maliki and Badr Organization leader Hadi Al-Ameri if both figures continue obstructing federal efforts to disarm armed factions.

The study, authored by former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State David Schenker and reported by the 964 Network, argues that the two veteran political leaders—who collectively command 47 parliamentary seats within the ruling Coordination Framework—remain entrenched in maximalist positions rather than facilitating genuine state control over weapons, particularly following high-profile cross-border drone strikes against regional energy targets.

The analysis highlights that while Al-Maliki previously pledged to defuse factional tensions and avert collisions with Baghdad’s sovereign agenda, Iranian-backed groups within the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) subsequently launched an explosive drone barrage on September 10 targeting Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude pipeline near Yanbu, Riyadh, and Medina.

The assault, which temporarily disrupted up to 4–5 million barrels per day of transit to the Red Sea, directly undermined Coordination Framework claims of having neutralized escalation risks, exposing the fragility of domestic political assurances.

Schenker notes that Al-Maliki narrowly escaped U.S. Treasury designations during the first Trump administration and warns that continued efforts to replace disarmament with ambiguous “containment” models—akin to Lebanese political formulas surrounding Hezbollah—should trigger direct U.S. financial designations against both Al-Maliki and Al-Ameri.

The policy paper comes as Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi approaches his self-imposed September 30 deadline to monopolize arms under sovereign command—a date that coincides with the scheduled conclusion of the U.S.-led International Coalition’s mission in Iraq.

While moderate factions like Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq and Kata’ib Imam Ali offered preliminary disarmament concessions, and Muqtada Al-Sadr agreed to absorb Saraya Al-Salam into the regular military, hardline elements led by Kata’ib Hezbollah, Harakat Hezbollah Al-Nujaba, and Kata’ib Sayyid Al-Shuhada have openly resisted.

Bolstered by summer visits from IRGC Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani, these groups have conditioned disarmament on non-starter demands, including dissolving the constitutionally recognized Kurdish Peshmerga, expelling Turkish forces, and enshrining PMF benefits by statute, while proposing unacceptable workarounds such as storing heavy weaponry in Iran or maintaining private depots under a nominal two-year activity freeze.

World.title: Iraq’s University of Technology explores academic partnerships in Spain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s University of Technology conducted high-level academic discussions on Saturday, September 19, 2026, with Spain’s University of Seville and University of Granada, aiming to broaden bilateral research cooperation, facilitate student and faculty exchanges, and launch joint scientific projects.

According to an official university statement carried by INA, the institutional visit was led by the President of the University of Technology, Mohsen Nouri Hamza, heading a senior academic delegation as part of the institution’s broader strategy to expand global academic engagement.

At the University of Granada, Hamza met with University Rector Pedro Mercado Pacheco to review frameworks for institutional collaboration and advance a draft comprehensive Global Agreement designed to govern future academic and scientific ties.

The delegation held additional technical sessions with Irene Pedreira Romero, Director of International Projects and Networks, and Leandro Di Stasi, Director of Internationalization at the International School for Postgraduate Studies.

Deliberations centered on establishing joint research initiatives and leveraging opportunities under the European Union’s Erasmus+ program to facilitate bilateral mobility for researchers, instructors, and graduate students, including hosting Iraqi postgraduate candidates in Spanish laboratories to carry out specialized thesis work.

The mission to the University of Seville focused on technical and engineering disciplines aligned with national development priorities. Talks concentrated on joint projects in renewable energy, industrial catalysts, advanced materials, structural engineering, and sustainable architectural design.

The Iraqi delegation—which included Dean of the College of Architecture Abbas Ali Hamza, Dean of the College of Electromechanical Engineering Ghassan Abdul Hussein Bilal, Materials Engineering faculty member Mohammed Al-Zuhairi, and Electromechanical Engineering faculty member Sundus Samir Jumaa—agreed to establish specialized bilateral research teams aimed at supporting sustainable development through academic innovation.

World.title: Four key clashes conclude Iraq Stars League matchday 8 on Saturday
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Four decisive fixtures will wrap up Matchday 8 of the Iraq Stars League on Saturday evening, September 19, 2026, setting the stage for high-stakes clashes spanning the title chase, mid-table consolidation, and redemption campaigns.

The evening action kicks off at 6:45 PM Baghdad time with two simultaneous fixtures. Ghaz Al-Shamal takes on Newroz in an encounter where both clubs will battle to secure maximum points and strengthen their footholds in the league standings. World.title: US dollar surges past 160,000 IQD amid US liquidity pressures and market slump
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar crossed the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency markets during opening trading on Saturday, September 19, 2026, marking a sharp depreciation of the domestic currency as market liquidity contracted under geopolitical and fiscal strains.

Bureaus in Baghdad posted selling prices of 160,000 dinars per $100 against buying rates of 159,500 dinars, while trading in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, reflected a parallel surge, settling at 159,650 dinars for sale and 159,100 dinars for purchase.

The widening spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s official peg of 131,000 dinars follows reports of heightened U.S. Treasury pressure and restrictions on monthly physical cash shipments from Iraq’s oil revenue reserves held at the U.S. Federal Reserve.

Washington has reportedly conditioned the continuity of unhindered dollar liquidity flows on Baghdad’s progress in disarming Iran-aligned armed factions and meeting the critical September 30 deadline, which coincides with the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military presence.

The resulting cash shortage has fueled market speculation, with local traders and currency dealers warning that selling rates could climb toward the 170,000-dinar mark if physical inflows remain constrained.

The monetary volatility has begun depressing consumer sentiment across the country ahead of the month-end deadline. Households across Iraqi governorates have visibly shifted toward precautionary saving and defensive spending, prioritizing essential food commodities while curtailing expenditures on discretionary goods and leisure services.

Foot traffic and commercial turnover have contracted noticeably across cafes, restaurants, and retail markets—even extending to school stationery vendors preparing for the upcoming academic term—choking domestic cash flow and deepening liquidity bottlenecks across the real economy.

World.title: Iraq Customs clarifies duties on pharmaceuticals, vitamins, and supplements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi General Authority of Customs asserted on Friday evening, September 18, 2026, that the formal classification of imported commodities and the determination of their corresponding Harmonized System (HS) codes and tariff bands remain the exclusive legal jurisdiction of the customs authority.

In a statement received IraqiNews.com, the authority clarified the operative tariff schedules for healthcare products, noting that certified pharmaceutical products are levied at a baseline duty of 0.5%, while vitamins and dietary supplements face duties of either 5% or 10% based on technical categorization.

Customs regulators emphasized that receiving testing clearances or regulatory approvals from the Ministry of Health does not automatically classify a product as a pharmaceutical medicine for border assessment purposes.

The authority underlined that health sector certifications fulfill domestic safety compliance requirements, whereas border taxation, HS code designation, and duty assessments are determined strictly through official statutory tariff tables and active customs regulations.

Under the declared tariff structure, conventional pharmaceuticals formally categorized under recognized medical subheadings qualify for the lower 0.5% rate.

Conversely, vitamins and nutritional supplements are evaluated individually based on their specific chemical formulation, physical composition, and technical commodity descriptions, subjecting them to standard 5% or 10% duty brackets rather than pharmaceutical exemptions.

The authority reiterated that brand names, marketing designations, or laboratory review bodies do not dictate tariff bands, which rely solely on technical HS documentation.

The regulatory clarification addresses recurring friction between border revenue authorities and the domestic healthcare market regarding import costs. In January 2026, the General Authority of Customs confirmed a 1% tariff adjustment on medical supplies, dismissing claims of a ten-fold duty increase flagged by the Iraqi Syndicate of Pharmacists as an unintentional clerical error.

The latest customs advisory establishes clear statutory boundaries between health testing protocols and fiscal border valuations, maintaining firm oversight over revenue collection on non-essential health and wellness supplements entering the country.

World.title: Amit Shah wants UCC in all NDA states by 2029. What will JD(U) do in Bihar?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Is the implementation of the

emerging as a new point of contention between the Bharatiya Janata Party and one of its oldest allies, Janata Dal (United)?

The question has come into focus after Union home minister Amit Shah's assertion that UCC would be implemented in all 21 NDA-ruled states before the next Lok Sabha elections prompted differing reactions within the JD(U).

The issue surfaced after Shah, during his visit to Mumbai, put a timeline on BJP's plan to implement one of its longstanding ideological objectives before the 2029 Lok Sabha polls.

"Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in several states and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states, we will introduce the UCC before 2029," Shah said.

Shah's message, however, drew a different response from some JD(U) leaders in Bihar.

JD(U) general secretary and former minister Shyam Rajak said his party did not favour implementing UCC in the state.

"Our stand on the issue was made clear by our leader way back. He had said that although our party was supporting the UCC Bill in the Parliament, it was not in favour of implementing the same in Bihar," Rajak said.

"The chief minister may be of the BJP but the government is being run with the help of allies...





our stand is clear, the question of implementing UCC in Bihar does not arise," he added.

However, Bihar deputy chief minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary, who is considered to be a close ally of former chief minister Nitish Kumar, adopted a more cautious stance and said the party would first study the legislation and would not oppose it "for no reason" if its provisions were found to be unexceptionable.

"As of now, we are not aware of the details of the legislation on UCC.

Let it be placed before us. If we find there is nothing objectionable, why shall we oppose it without any reason? And if there are points of concern, these will be conveyed to the Union home minister," Chaudhary said.

JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha has also indicated that party leaders would discuss the issue with Shah.

For now, therefore, JD(U)'s stand is not entirely clear. While some leaders have spoken against implementing UCC in Bihar, remarks by senior leaders such as Chaudhary and Jha have left scope for the party to examine the proposed provisions before taking a final position.

The party has historically favoured wider consultations and consensus on the issue.

What is UCC

India already has uniform criminal laws and common civil laws covering matters such as taxation, contracts and negotiable instruments. However, when it comes to personal laws such as marriage, divorce and inheritance of property, different religious communities follow laws based on their respective traditions and practices.

Article 44 under the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Constitution says that the State shall endeavour to secure a UCC for citizens throughout India.

"The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India," the Constitution says.

A UCC broadly seeks to provide a common legal framework for citizens in matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and succession.

BJP's old promise

The Uniform Civil Code has been a longstanding part of the BJP's political agenda and has featured repeatedly in the party's election manifestos over the years.

The party has repeatedly included the issue in its election manifestos, arguing that a common civil code would ensure equality before law and strengthen women's rights in matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and adoption.

Matters such as marriage, divorce, adoption, wills, intestacy and succession fall in the Concurrent List, allowing both the Centre and state governments to make laws on them.

In 2022, then Union law minister Kiren Rijiju also informed the Rajya Sabha that states were empowered to legislate on these subjects.

"Article 44 of the Constitution provides that the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India," Rijiju had said in a written reply.

"Personal laws such as intestacy and succession; wills; joint family and partition; marriage and divorce, relate to Entry 5 of List-III-Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, and hence, the States are also empowered to legislate upon them," he had added.

This has allowed BJP-ruled states to take the state route on UCC.

Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to implement a state-specific Uniform Civil Code on January 27, 2025.

Since then, UCC Bills have also been passed by the assemblies of BJP-ruled Gujarat, Assam and Madhya Pradesh. As of mid-September, the Bills in these three states were awaiting the President's assent.

Other NDA-ruled states are at different stages of considering or preparing their own legislation.

Shah's latest remarks have now put a 2029 timeline on that process for all NDA-ruled states.

Why UCC needs careful balancing for JD(U)

For JD(U), the issue comes with both political and ideological considerations.

Nitish Kumar has long maintained that a reform such as UCC should not be pushed without broad consultation and consensus, particularly given India's social and religious diversity.

There is also an electoral dimension.

Within the NDA in Bihar, JD(U) has traditionally sought support across a social coalition that includes Extremely Backward Classes, women and sections of minorities.

While its support among Muslims has weakened over the years, the party has continued to reach out to the community.

Muslims constitute around 17.7% of Bihar's population, according to the state's caste survey. Recent electoral data cited by The Indian Express suggests that only a relatively small section of Muslim voters backed the NDA in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, underlining the challenge for JD(U) in retaining support among the community while remaining part of the BJP-led alliance.

In the 2025 assembly election, JD(U) fielded four Muslim candidates, but only Mohammad Zama Khan won from the Chainpur seat.

The political setting has also changed since that election.

The NDA won 202 of Bihar's 243 assembly seats, with the BJP emerging as the single-largest party with 89 seats and JD(U) winning 85.

Nitish Kumar is also no longer chief minister, with BJP's Samrat Choudhary now heading the NDA government.

JD(U), however, remains one of its two principal constituents.

This makes the UCC question an important one for the alliance: BJP has put a timeline on a longstanding policy commitment, while JD(U) has traditionally stressed consultation before any such move.

When JD(U) differed with BJP

Although an ally of BJP, JD(U) has not always agreed with it on politically sensitive issues.

On UCC itself, Nitish Kumar has long cautioned against hurried implementation.

In January 2017, as Bihar chief minister, he returned the Law Commission's questionnaire on UCC, arguing that there was insufficient clarity about what the proposed code would contain and calling for wider consultations with affected groups.

Nitish argued that diverse customs and practices had existed for centuries and that any effort towards a common code should be based on consensus rather than simply imposed.

JD(U) has also differed from the BJP on issues such as the Triple Talaq Bill and the abrogation of Article 370.

In 2019, JD(U) opposed the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Bill, commonly known as the Triple Talaq Bill. The party objected particularly to the provision making instant triple talaq a criminal offence, arguing that the legislation could create "a lack of trust" in society. Its MPs walked out of the Lok Sabha debate and later abstained during the Rajya Sabha proceedings.

In August 2019, the party also opposed the Modi government's decision to abrogate the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 and reorganise the former state into two Union Territories. JD(U) MPs staged a walkout when the measures were introduced in Parliament.

However, it struck a reconciliatory note later and said that once the law had come into force, it should be abided by all.

These differences did not, by themselves, prevent the BJP and JD(U) from working together.

The two allies have in the past maintained separate positions on some issues while continuing their political partnership.

UCC could similarly depend on what form a proposed law for Bihar eventually takes and whether the allies are able to arrive at a common position.

Mahagathbandhan's offer to Nitish

Amid the debate over UCC, Congress and Rashtriya Janata Dal have taken the opportunity to invite Nitish Kumar to join the opposition alliance.

RJD MLA Bhai Virendra asked Nitish to break ties with the BJP and form a new government with its support, saying the parties shared a socialist political tradition.

The RJD MLA alleged that Nitish was surrounded by people who were "hellbent on ruining his political career" and said, "We urge Nitish Kumar ji to walk out of the NDA and form a govt with our support."

Former Bihar Congress president and Rajya Sabha member Akhilesh Prasad Singh also extended an invitation to Nitish to join the Mahagathbandhan, saying Nitish had long been associated with socialist politics.

"It is the agenda of the BJP and the RSS. Several allies of the NDA may not agree with it, and Nitish certainly should not agree with it.

He has always been associated with social concerns and socialism, so I do not think he can ever agree with this," Singh said.

"Why would Congress have any objection to that? If he leaves, Congress will always welcome him," he added.

For now, however, the differing remarks on UCC do not necessarily point to a larger crisis within the Bihar NDA.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

JD(U)'s final position remains open. Some of its leaders have opposed implementation in Bihar, while others have said the party should first see the proposed legislation and discuss its concerns with the BJP leadership.

Shah, meanwhile, has set a clear target of introducing UCC in all NDA-ruled states before 2029.

It remains to be seen whether Bihar eventually follows that roadmap and, if it does, what shape the proposed law takes after consultations between the two allies.

World.title: Ajmal is Assam CM’s ‘108’ service, says Gaurav Gogoi
World.content:
GUWAHATI

Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi on Sunday (September 20, 2026) said All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) chief Mohammed Badruddin Ajmal was Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma’s “108”.

The number refers to the Emergency Response Service, a toll-free 24/7 helpline in the country, primarily for ambulances.

Addressing a party rally in Nagaon district’s Dhing for the Nagaon parliamentary by-election, Mr. Gogoi alleged a “secret alliance” between the two main leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the AIUDF, respectively, in Assam.

The election to the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat is scheduled for October 6. The bypoll became necessary after Pradyut Bordoloi, who won the constituency for the second time in 2024, quit Congress and joined the BJP. He contested and won the Dispur Assembly seat for the BJP in April 2026.

“Badruddin Ajmal is contesting the Nagaon seat to benefit the BJP. He is Himanta Biswa Sarma’s 108,” Mr. Gogoi said while campaigning for Congress candidate Sibamoni Bora.

Mr. Gogoi further said the AIUDF had a different candidate in mind for the Nagaon constituency. However, its chief nominated himself after finding out that the Congress had fielded a strong candidate in Ms. Bora.

He indicated Ajmal’s candidature was part of the BJP’s strategy to counter Congress in minority-dominated constituencies like Nagaon.

The Nagaon by-election is expected to witness a three-cornered contest involving Congress’s Ms. Bora, the BJP’s bureaucrat-turned-politician Devasish Sharma, and the AIUDF’s Mr. Ajmal.

The other candidates are Inamul Huda of the Revolutionary Communist Party of India (Rashik Bhatt), Barnali Sharma of the Socialist Unity Centre of India (Communist), Hafiz Burhanuddin of the National Road Map Party of India, and nine independents.

The Assam Trinamool Congress nominated academic Abdul Salam, but withdrew his candidature after the Election Commission of India froze the party name and symbol.

World.title: Two NIT-K professors get Eminent Engineer awards
World.content:
Two professors of the National Institute of Technology - Karnataka (NIT-K), Surathkal, have been conferred with the Eminent Engineer Award – 2026 in the academician category by The Institution of Engineers (India), Karnataka State Centre.

They are G.S. Dwarakish, Professor (Higher Academic Grade), Department of Water Resources and Ocean Engineering, and Basavaraju Manu, Professor, Department of Civil Engineering.

They received the award from Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar at the 59th Engineers’ Day celebration held at the IEI Karnataka State Centre, Bengaluru, recently.

Prof. Dwarakish was recognised for his contributions to water resources, coastal engineering, remote sensing, and GIS. Prof. Manu was recognised for his research in water and wastewater treatment, supported by peer-reviewed publications, citations, and patents, an NIT-K release said.

World.title: Activists accuse Mumbai cops of pressuring people, raiding venues to stop Umar Khalid film screening
World.content:
Activists Shrishti Khanna and Prashant Pundir have alleged that Mumbai police got the screening of a documentary on Umar Khalid, a former JNU students' union leader arrested in 2020 in connection with the Delhi riots case, cancelled after raiding the venue where it was to be held.

In a post on Instagram, Ms. Khanna said they were were supposed to screen "Prisoner No. 626710 Is Present" in solidarity with Mr. Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, also in jail since 2020, here on September 19.

"Mumbai Police has crossed all levels of cowardice! They have raided our original venue for the Umar Khalid screening as well, which had already been cancelled for us due to fear.

"For context, they threatened the venue manager of our final venue yesterday and got the screening cancelled. We even mentioned publicly that the screening is cancelled, but Mumbai Police still raided the original venue today, which had already been cancelled on us due to fear, just in case, to make sure the truth about Umar Khalid and his unjust incarceration is suppressed," Mr. Pundir said in a post on X on Saturday (September 19, 2026).

There are groups in civilian clothes lurking around our original venue to still make sure no screening happens, Mr. Pundir said.

Ms. Khanna also alleged Mumbai police personnel are showing up in civilian clothes to intimidate venues to cancel the documentary screening in solidarity with Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam.

"Our second venue was visited by police, first in civilian clothes and later in a police van. The venue manager was threatened and pressured to cancel the screening, and it was eventually cancelled. But it did not stop there," Ms. Khanna said.

The police also showed up at another well-known venue in Bandra that they had only spoken to while looking for possible spaces, Ms. Khanna said.

"It didn't work out with them. They arrived this morning in civilian clothes, already had information about the screening, and told the venue to cancel it," Mr. Khanna claimed.

"Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, centres on Mr. Khalid, a former Jawaharlal Nehru University research scholar who was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy behind the northeast Delhi riots.

Mr. Khalid has been charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and other provisions in the case and has remained in custody since his arrest.

Incidentally, the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) has opposed the screening of the documentary in various parts of the country stating that public exhibition of an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption had been obtained.

World.title: Bengaluru: POCSO case accused found dead
World.content:
A 49-year-old physical education teacher, who was arrested in a Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act case, died after allegedly jumping from the third floor of the Bengaluru South district Superintendent of Police’s office complex in Ramanagara on Sunday (September 20).

The deceased has been identified as S. Shashidhar, a native of Chapparadahalli in Kottur taluk of Vijayanagara district. He was working at a private school under the jurisdiction of the Akkur police station in Channapatna taluk.

According to the police, Shashidhar was accused of sexually assaulting children at the school. The Ramanagara Women’s Police Station registered a POCSO case three days ago and arrested him.

After being taken into custody, Shashidhar was questioned by the police. On Sunday morning, he underwent a medical examination before being brought to the SP’s office for completion of formalities ahead of his remand in judicial custody.

The police said his fingerprints were recorded on the third floor of the office. While he was being escorted back to the police vehicle, Shashidhar allegedly pushed aside a constable accompanying him and suddenly jumped from the third floor.

He sustained serious injuries in the fall and was rushed to a nearby district hospital. However, he died after reportedly failing to respond to treatment, a police officer said.

Further investigation is on.
